responsibilitiesHtml:
About Avoca

Avoca is a Y Combinator–backed vertical AI company transforming how home services businesses convert demand into revenue. Home services is a $500B+ industry, and more than 95% of revenue still flows through call centers—where missed calls, slow follow-up, and operational chaos cause massive leakage. Avoca fixes this.
Our platform captures and converts every opportunity by:

  • Answering 100% of inbound calls with real-time Voice AI that books jobs instantly

  • Automating outbound engagement across calls, SMS, and multi-channel follow-up

  • Orchestrating scheduling & dispatch through deep CRM integrations (e.g., ServiceTitan)

  • Leveling up teams with coaching tools and analytics

The result: 15–40% more booked jobs in the first 30 days, protected ad spend, and dramatically simplified operations.

We move 2–3× faster than any competitor, ship new products constantly, and work hand-in-hand with the largest HVAC, plumbing, electrical, and home service brands in the country.

We’ve raised $37M led by Kleiner Perkins, with additional backing from Amplify Partners, Alt Capital, Jack Altman, and other tier-1 investors.
We’ve grown the team from ~15 → ~70 and are continuing to scale rapidly.

This is a rare chance to join at an inflection point—where product-market fit is clear, the TAM is massive, and foundational systems are still being built.

About the Role

We’re hiring Product Engineers—generalist full-stack builders who thrive at the intersection of engineering, product, and real-world operational impact.

You’ll ship features end-to-end across a fast-expanding platform (inbound voice AI, outbound engines, dispatch, speed-to-lead, coaching), working directly with founders and forward-deployed engineers to solve high-stakes problems for customers.

This is a high-ownership, high-velocity environment where what you build is used immediately by thousands of technicians, CSRs, and operators—and directly drives revenue for our customers.

What You’ll Do

  • Own features end-to-end — design, build, launch, measure, iterate

  • Build real-time AI-driven user experiences, backend services, and data workflows

  • Turn customer feedback into product improvements through rapid iteration

  • Work closely with Product, Customer Success, FDEs, and GTM teams

  • Hold a high bar for testing, reliability, and operational excellence

  • Navigate ambiguous requirements and ruthlessly prioritize impact

  • Contribute to a fast-moving engineering culture with massive surface area to own

Why Avoca

  • Category-defining vertical AI company in a massive underserved market

  • 10× ARR growth year-over-year and expanding rapidly across mid-market and enterprise

  • Work directly with technical founders from the MIT Voice AI Lab

  • Ship 2–3× faster than competitors—engineers take features from idea → production in weeks

  • Real ownership: the work you do directly impacts revenue for thousands of businesses

  • Join at the moment when core product, customer, and GTM systems are being built
requirementsHtml:
• Experience: 5+ years preferred, ideally with full-stack engineering background and experience owning end-to-end, product-critical initiatives.
  • AI Expertise: Strong familiarity with AI, LLMs, or AI-assisted systems.
  • Product Ownership: Ability to own features from backend to frontend, iterate based on customer feedback, and drive outcomes measured by impact.
  • Collaboration: Comfortable working closely with Product, Customer Success, and GTM teams.
  • Engineering Quality & Autonomy: Maintain high code quality (testing, monitoring, reliability), prioritize effectively, and operate with autonomy in dynamic environments.
  • Work Environment: Full-time, in-person role based in NYC; startup or small-company experience preferred but not required; minimal formal education requirements but high talent bar.
  • Computer Science Undergraduate Degree from a top school

responsibilitiesHtml:
About AfterQuery

AfterQuery builds the training data and evaluation infrastructure that frontier AI labs use to improve their models. They work with all five of the world's leading AI labs to design high-signal datasets and run rigorous evaluations that go beyond static benchmarks. One of the fastest-growing companies in their YC batch, backed by Y Combinator, BoxGroup, Lightspeed, Warburg Pincus, Silver Lake, and Index Ventures, with $30M raised at a $300M valuation.

About the Role

This is a founding-level role sitting directly at the intersection of technical execution and strategic leadership. You'll own high-impact initiatives end-to-end, from requirements through delivery, managing teams of software engineers, data scientists, and ML specialists while shipping production code yourself. One week you're scoping a dataset pipeline for a frontier lab; the next you're debugging infrastructure under live pressure or designing quality control systems that power $10M+ contracts. You'll work directly with the founding team and interface with research leads at Anthropic, OpenAI, and the other labs shaping the frontier. Success means compressing cycle time, building systems that scale to multiple labs simultaneously, and becoming the person the founders trust with their highest-priority, most ambiguous problems.

What You'll Own

  • Own end-to-end technical initiatives: scoping requirements, building solutions, managing experts through delivery, and shipping code yourself when it unblocks the team.

  • Design and build technical infrastructure and tooling for dataset generation, quality control, and delivery pipelines supporting multiple concurrent frontier lab contracts.

  • Manage and mentor teams of software engineers, data scientists, and ML specialists on high-priority campaigns; set technical direction and hold the bar for execution velocity.

  • Interface directly with research teams at leading AI labs to understand their needs, translate them into technical specs, and ensure delivery meets their standards.

  • Debug production issues live under pressure; rapidly context-switch between hands-on engineering, team leadership, and strategic problem-solving.

  • Support the founding team on whatever moves the needle most: from building new internal tools to closing technical details on major contracts to hiring the next engineers.

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. Ship production code regularly in Python; demonstrate proficiency with data pipelines, APIs, or ML/AI tooling in real systems you've built.

  2. Manage and mentor teams of technical experts; show a track record of setting direction, holding people accountable, and improving performance.

  3. Extreme high agency and founder-level intensity; comfortable operating with ambiguous scope, making high-stakes calls on incomplete information, and shipping fast.

  4. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, engineering equivalent, or demonstrated ability to ship substantial technical projects; top-tier technical pedigree preferred (FAANG, frontier AI lab, quantitative trading, founding engineer).

  5. Articulate clearly why you want this role and what draws you to frontier AI; evidence of genuine engagement with the research community.

Nice-to-Have

  • Prior founding engineer, early-stage startup, or founder experience; shows the agency and autonomy the role demands.

  • Background at a frontier AI lab, FAANG engineering team, or quantitative trading firm; signals the technical depth and execution pace.

  • Direct experience building infrastructure for data generation, annotation pipelines, or model evaluation systems.

  • Passion for AI research and active engagement with frontier AI labs (read papers, follow research, have opinions on what matters).

responsibilitiesHtml:
About Verita AI

Verita AI is building a job matching platform that connects domain experts with high-paying data training opportunities at the world's leading AI labs. Think of it as a job marketplace built specifically for the people powering frontier AI: experts in engineering, creativity, finance, and beyond, matched directly with the training opportunities that need their expertise most.

The platform makes contributing to AI training feel intuitive, rewarding, and even fun. Built-in leaderboards, gamification, and progression systems turn high-quality work into recognition and growth. The matching engine routes experts to the projects best suited to their skills, and the talent management tooling measures, ranks, and rewards performance at scale.

Verita recently raised a $6 million seed round led by Kindred Ventures.

About the Role

Verita is hiring Strategic Project Leads to own the end-to-end execution of high-stakes AI data projects for top-tier frontier AI lab clients. SPLs are the primary point of contact for leading AI labs, orchestrating complex workflows, managing teams of expert contributors, and ensuring every deliverable meets the highest standards of quality and efficiency.

This is a high-impact, operationally intensive role where you balance client relationships, team coordination, process optimization, and real-time problem solving. Average SPL workload is 2-3 projects concurrently or one marquee project, managing 7-8 figure contracts per quarter.

What You'll Own

  • Serve as the main point of contact for top AI lab customers, building deep trust and long-term partnerships

  • Understand client objectives and translate them into executable project plans

  • Design and manage large-scale data pipelines from client specification through final delivery

  • Recruit, vet, onboard, and manage teams of expert contributors at scale

  • Mentor and develop Strategic Project Associates on your projects

  • Own 2-3 projects concurrently or one marquee project at any given time

Requirements

Must-Have

  • 3+ years full-time experience in a strategic project lead or equivalent role at Mercor, Scale AI, or a comparable frontier human data company

  • Full-time employment history. No contractor or annotator experience counts toward the bar.

  • Proven track record of managing complex, multi-stakeholder projects with 7+ figure contract value

  • Experience working directly with clients in a customer-facing capacity

  • Comfort owning end-to-end project execution under an intense pace and high stakes

  • Based in SF or willing to relocate. 5 days in office, 996 schedule.

As Account Executive at Kobalt Labs, you'll own the full sales cycle — from sourcing to close — selling AI-powered compliance and risk automation to banks, credit unions, and fintechs. responsibilitiesHtml:
About Known

Known is a matchmaker that talks to users and supports them like a friend. The mission is to empower humanity by applying general intelligence to human connection. Users join by telling Known their life story through an AI voice agent, with new users averaging 27 minutes of conversation, giving Known a uniquely intimate context to make real matches. Launched in February, the release video got 2 million views on Twitter, 10,000 people signed up in San Francisco alone in the first days, and the app's concurrency shocked the infrastructure. The team has since hardened the platform and is now rolling out paid live dates to a wider population. Raising a Series A in the next six months. $10M seed raised in November, backed by Forerunner Ventures (Eurie Kim and Kirsten Green, investors behind Decagon, Faire, and Oura), NFX, and Pear VC. A team of engineers who have built some of the most widely used AI-driven consumer products including Uber, Uber Eats, Afterpay, and Cash App. In-person in Cow Hollow, San Francisco.

About the Role

Known is looking for a React Native mobile engineer who builds consumer products with the care and craft of an artisan. Building Known is an exercise in design. The goal is to be the Apple of dating, and the engineers here steward that quality. This is a product-led, user-obsessed role where you will work on complex audio and voice features that make the Known experience feel distinctly human.

Known has proven product-market fit and demand that broke their infrastructure on day one. The platform is now hardened and the company is entering its growth phase. They need a mobile engineer who can elevate the product as they expand into more cities and head into a Series A round.

You are building a consumer product with a genuinely novel technical challenge at the core, real-time AI voice and audio features, for a company that already has 10,000 users who loved it so much they crashed the app. The mission is to design intelligence that leads to a million marriages.

What You'll Own

  • Own and elevate the Known mobile app end-to-end in React Native across iOS and Android

  • Build complex audio and voice features that make the Known experience feel human and intentional

  • Take products from concept to production with a high degree of autonomy and ownership

  • Work directly with the founding team on architectural and product decisions

  • Steward the quality and craft of a consumer product that is held to Apple-level design standards

  • Contribute to the platform as Known scales from hundreds of users to millions

Requirements

Must-Have

Technical

  • 2 to 6 years of production React Native experience. This is the single most important requirement

  • Has shipped and maintained a React Native app to both iOS and Android in production, not just a React web app

  • Experience with complex audio or voice features in a mobile context is a strong differentiator

  • Full-stack capability to take features end-to-end when needed

  • Has worked at a company where React Native was the primary mobile framework, such as Discord, early Airbnb, early Instacart, or equivalent

Execution and Ownership

  • High agency, works with autonomy, and does not wait for specs

  • Detail-oriented to a fault, cares about the feel and quality of the product as much as the functionality

  • Has worked at a startup through at least one phase shift, Series A, Series B, or equivalent growth transition

  • User-obsessed, thinks about how real people experience the product, not just how the code works

Location

  • In-person, Cow Hollow, San Francisco

Nice-to-Have

  • Consumer mobile app experience at a unicorn-stage company: Airbnb, Discord, Instacart, or similar

  • Has shipped an Android and iOS app simultaneously using React Native

  • Teaching or TA background in mobile app development (e.g., taught app dev at Stanford), signals deep React Native fundamentals

  • Experience with voice AI, audio streaming, or real-time communication features

Who Will Thrive Here

Someone who:

  • Takes genuine pride in the craft of mobile product development, not just shipping

  • Is excited about the mission of using AI to create a real human connection

  • Has the rare combination of strong React Native fundamentals and consumer product instincts

  • Wants to be part of building something that could genuinely change how people find relationships

Sphinx builds AI analysts that work inside browsers, APIs, and internal systems just like humans, automating AML, KYC, KYB, and transaction monitoring end to end. The product helps banks and fintechs eliminate 90% of manual work, cut compliance costs by 4x, and make onboarding instantaneous. The team has won every single deal they have competed for, including seven-figure contracts with leading banks.

About the Role

Sphinx is hiring a Founding Account Executive to own the full sales cycle from first touch to signed contract. Until now, sales has been founder-led; the company is now at the point where they need someone to build the pipeline, run the full cycle, and lay the foundation for a sales organization that scales. This is a builder seat, not a quota-carrying seat with a playbook handed to you.

What You'll Own

  • Own the full sales cycle from first touch to signed contract: prospecting, discovery, demos, negotiation, and close

  • Bring in new banks, fintechs, and MSBs across the US, Canada, Europe, and LatAm

  • Design the sales playbook, comp structures, and processes that let the team scale

  • Build Sphinx's sales organization alongside the CEO, including hiring the first AEs behind you

  • Partner with Dean and the GTM team to generate, qualify, and refine leads into a predictable pipeline

  • Shape pricing, packaging, territory planning, and competitive positioning

Must-Have

  1. 3-5+ years of enterprise sales experience closing contracts in the $100K to $1M+ range

  2. Prior sales experience in banks, large fintechs, or financial services institutions

  3. Full-cycle ownership: prospecting, discovery, demos, negotiation, and close

  4. Comfort with multi-stakeholder buying committees, procurement, and legal cycles

  5. Hunter mentality: builds pipeline, cold-calls confidently, creates opportunities

  6. Builder mindset, excited to write the playbook rather than execute against one

  7. Willing to relocate to San Francisco or already based there

Nice-to-Have

  • Existing network at banks, compliance consultancies, or large fintechs

  • Prior work at AML RightSource, Guidehouse, Protiviti, or comparable compliance consultancies

  • Prior sales at compliance tech, KYC/AML/KYB platforms, or financial crime infrastructure

  • Experience building a sales playbook from scratch at a Series A or B startup

Compensation & Benefits

  • Base: $150,000 - $200,000

  • OTE: $300,000 (50/50 base/variable at the $150K base point, sliding to ~65/35 at the $200K base point)

Interview Process

  • Screening call (fit & motivation)

  • Interview #1, in the office if possible.

  • Case study in the office.

  • Offer

responsibilitiesHtml:
ABOUT ARAVALLI CAPITAL

Aravalli Capital is a multi-strategy credit investment platform that builds software infrastructure to power how it invests, monitors, and reports. Small team, high ownership, direct access to senior investment and analytics leadership. You will help define how a modern credit firm operates at the systems level, from the ground up.

About the Role

Aravalli Capital is hiring an AI Systems Engineer - Credit Analyst to be embedded directly within the investment firm. You will not be expected to arrive with deep credit expertise, but you will be expected to have enough financial and analytical context to reason about the domain, understand why outputs need to be checked and validated, and build systems that actually work rather than brute-forcing problems through an LLM.

This is a software and AI systems role with broad ownership. You will build AI agent systems, automate manual analytical processes, handle real-world financial datasets, and deliver clear outputs for both internal teams and investors. The team values process thinking over output dumping. They want engineers who can explain every step of what they built, why they made each decision, and what checks they put in place to validate that the system is working correctly.

What You'll Own

  • Build AI agent systems for deal diligence, portfolio surveillance, and analytical workflows

  • Develop internal tooling that automates and replaces manual analytical processes

  • Build and maintain data pipelines handling large, messy, real-world financial datasets

  • Design a refactorable analytical infrastructure that evolves as investment requirements change

  • Deliver clear outputs, including dashboards, reports, and interfaces for internal teams and investors

  • Document your process clearly and be able to walk through every decision you made and every check you built in

REQUIREMENTS

Must-Have

  1. 2 to 6 years of experience with strong Python engineering skills. Production-grade systems, not just notebooks or LLM-piped outputs

  2. Finance or credit analytical background. Has worked at a lending fintech such as Affirm, Klarna, Pagaya, Upgrade, or Upstart, or has 1 to 4 years of experience in a junior Wall Street or credit analyst role. Enough domain knowledge to reason about the outputs being produced, not just the code

  3. Demonstrated experience building AI agents or agentic workflows, including multi-agent orchestration, RAG pipelines, and LLM integration. Critically, can explain the full process between problem and output, including the checks, validations, and decisions made along the way

  4. Collaborative and coachable. Can receive feedback on outputs without becoming defensive, willing to consider alternative directions even when their own output is not correct. This was the single cultural failure point on the benchmark candidate

Nice-to-Have

  • Lending fintech background at Affirm, Klarna, Pagaya, Upgrade, Upstart, Oportun, or equivalent

  • Prior exposure to structured credit, ABS, or private credit products

  • Experience with large, messy, real-world datasets and version control practices

  • Has written rule-based logic or checks inside AI pipelines rather than relying entirely on LLM outputs

As a Forward Engineer at Metis, you’ll be part of a tight-knit, product-driven team leveraging our training platform to deliver outcomes for customers. You’ll work across the stack, from low-level systems to user-facing features, to deliver resilient, high-performance products that power mission-critical AI workflows. We move fast, but we hold a very high bar for correctness, maintainability, and simplicity. You’ll be expected to write production-grade code, reason holistically about systems, and push the boundaries of what’s possible in applied AI engineering.

  • Experience with backend systems, distributed computing, or high-volume services

  • Strong communication abilities with a high bar for customer interaction

  • Ability to turn ambiguous product asks into simple, pragmatic solutions

  • Familiarity with system design, software engineering best practices, and debugging in production environments

  • Comfortable working across the stack — from APIs and orchestration to user-facing surfaces

About Contrario

Contrario (YC W25) is building an AI-powered recruiting marketplace that connects elite startup recruiters with fast-growing companies through software and operational tooling. We’ve raised $2.5M from Y Combinator and Nexus Venture Partners, with angels from Hudson River Trading, Stanford, and OpenAI. Our customers include 150+ YC and venture-backed startups hiring across engineering and GTM roles.

The Role

We’re hiring Talent Operators to join our team!

As a Talent Operator, you are the engine of our marketplace. You will run full-cycle recruiting for our partners while actively stress-testing Contrario’s internal AI and tooling. You’ll be on the front lines, mastering the recruiting landscape before transitioning into broader operational or leadership roles.

Once you master the recruitment landscape, we’ll increase your scope based on where you spike best. This could be account management, working with our recruiter network, or scaling internal systems.

This is a role for someone who loves to win, thrives in fast-paced environments, and wants to see their direct impact on a company’s bottom line every single day.

Compensation

  • Base is $80k–$110k, and total comp (OTE) is ~$140k-$170k+
    (earnings are uncapped)

Earnings-based compensation is directly tied to revenue generated off of successful placements.

Growth Path

We view the Talent Operator role as a proving ground for future leaders at Contrario. As an early team member, your path is based on where you "spike" and what you're passionate about:

  • Account Management: Own the end-to-end relationship with our partner companies and recruiters.

  • Recruitment Management: Scale and lead a team of Talent Operators as we grow.

  • Marketplace Operations: Drive the supply and demand strategy for our marketplace.

We are committed to investing in your growth. In exchange, we ask for high throughput, sharp judgment, and a "founder" mindset.

What You’ll Do

  • Master the Funnel: Source, screen, and manage candidates across multiple high-growth startup pipelines.

  • Product Feedback Loop: Be the primary "power user" of Contrario’s AI features, providing direct feedback to our engineering team to help shape the product.

  • Relationship Management: Act as a bridge between candidates and the elite startups we serve.

  • Build the Playbook: Help us refine our internal operations and recruiting systems as we scale from 200 to 1,000+ customers.

About You

  • 0-2 years in operations, recruiting, or other high-signal backgrounds (consulting, IB, etc.)

  • High agency and output-driven execution

  • Comfortable managing high-volume, fast-moving workloads

  • Low ego and highly coachable

  • Based in or relocating to San Francisco

About the interview

  1. Initial Screen (20–30 min) with Will, Chief of Staff.

  2. Take-Home Sourcing Exercise (2–3 hours, skippable)

  3. Team Panel Interviews

  4. On-Site / Working Session (1-2 days)

ABOUT THE COMPANY

Dynamo AI (YC W22) is an AI governance and cybersecurity company protecting the world's most advanced LLM deployments. ABOUT THE ROLE

As Federal Account Executive at Dynamo AI, you'll build the company's federal sales motion from the ground up, owning pipeline development, capture campaigns, and deal closure across the Department of Defense and Intelligence Community. You'll report directly to the Federal Implementation Leader and work without SDR support, reaching out directly to system integrators, program offices, and government agencies. This is not a civilian agency role; Dynamo's two federal beachheads are the Army and Air Force, and the ideal candidate has sold software or cybersecurity products directly into one or both. Base salary for this role is $100,000–$150,000 with a total OTE of $200,000–$300,000 depending on experience.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Build federal pipeline from scratch, identify, research, and pursue new opportunities across DoD and IC agencies through cold outreach, SAM.gov, conferences, and procurement boards

  • Lead capture campaigns end-to-end, pipeline development, positioning, teaming, proposal development, and contract execution

  • Cultivate relationships with acquisition leaders, program managers, system integrators, and innovation organizations, including DIU and AFWERX

  • Craft compelling, compliant responses to RFPs and RFIs via SAM.gov in partnership with solutions engineering and product teams

  • Shape requirements and influence early-stage opportunities through insight into mission gaps, emerging CONOPS, and acquisition timelines

  • Close complex, multi-stakeholder federal sales cycles — navigating DoD budgeting cycles, OTA vehicles, and system integrator partnerships to secure contracts

  • Network relentlessly at federal cybersecurity and AI events — building relationships with CISOs, PMs, and procurement leads in the D.C. area and beyond

  • Bring market feedback to leadership to help shape Dynamo's federal strategy, positioning, and partnerships

Must-Have

  • Ability to translate technical AI/ML, data security, and cloud infrastructure solutions into clear mission outcomes

  • Established network within the defense innovation ecosystem,  program offices, PEOs, acquisition commands, prime contractors, and system integrators

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, experience briefing senior leaders, and building consensus across diverse audiences

  • Based in the Washington, D.C. / Northern Virginia area, must be able to attend events and meetings on an impromptu basis

  • U.S. citizenship required, must be able to pass a background check

  • Willingness to travel 25–30% for conferences, on-site meetings, and industry events

Nice-to-Have

  • Existing network within the Department of Defense, Army, Air Force, or Intelligence Community

About Judgment Labs

Judgment Labs builds infrastructure for Agent Behavior Monitoring (ABM). While traditional observability focuses on logging exceptions and latency, ABM surfaces behavioral anomalies such as instruction drifts and context retrieval loss in scaled production environments. Hundreds of teams building autonomous agents rely on Judgment to understand how their systems are behaving post-deployment.

The team has raised $30M+ across two rounds in the past five months. Investors include Lightspeed, SV Angel, Valor Equity Partners, Nova Global, Chris Manning, Michael Ovitz, Michael Abbott, Cory Levy, and Kevin Hartz. The team is under 20 people and ships at 50+ company velocity, with Olympiad medalists, debate champions, and competitive athletes who bring that same intensity to company building. Everyone is either an ex-founder or a founder-to-be.

About the Role

Judgment Labs is hiring a Full-Stack Engineer to own the product experiences and agent infrastructure that make the agent improvement loop legible and actionable for engineering teams. This is not a role where you implement specs handed down: you will talk to customers, define what to build, build it, and iterate until it is great. The role spans from the data layer to the UI, including the agent swarm interfaces, verification platforms, and the SDK layer that lets developers summon Judgment mid-development. About 30% of the role is customer-facing.

What You'll Own

  • Shape how the Judgment Agent runs large-scale parallel investigations across thousands of production traces, merging failure modes, tool errors, regressions, and drift signals into a single actionable answer

  • Build the platform for verifying agent changes: hosted simulated environments for stateful agent evals, trajectory replay against changed agents, and monitors for unintended behavior

  • Design how engineers understand long traces, tool calls, decisions, and failures: making a thousand-step reasoning trajectory legible in minutes

  • Build the swarm UX so engineers can watch parallel investigations, redirect investigators that go down the wrong path, and consume findings without reading hundreds of reports

  • Own the improvement loop: the workflows that turn production trajectories into datasets, judges, and regression checks so the path from found problem to verified fix feels like one motion

  • Build and maintain the SDK and terminal-first experience so agent development sessions can summon Judgment as a subagent mid-development

  • Own platform infrastructure: workspaces, roles, permissions, billing, usage, and limits for teams running many agents across many environments

Must-Have

  1. Experience building and scaling end-to-end production systems, from data layer to UI

  2. Hands-on experience building with LLMs or agents, or demonstrable drive to get there fast

  3. Comfort working directly with customers to understand their needs and solve real-world problems (approximately 30% of the role is customer-facing)

  4. Strong technical problem-solving ability in fast-changing, ambiguous environments

  5. Excellent communication skills: clear, direct, and persuasive across technical and non-technical audiences

  6. Based in San Francisco or willing to relocate; 5 days per week in-person

Nice-to-Have

  • Prior evals, observability, or agent behavior-monitoring product experience

  • Strong engineering pedigree from a solid product company (e.g. Roblox, Snapchat, Tesla); top-tier infra background (e.g. Databricks) is a bonus

  • Prior forward-deployed or solutions engineering experience

  • Prior 0-to-1 startup experience as an early hire

  • Founder background or strong founder-to-be signal

  • Comfort across the full stack with backend and infrastructure weight

We work in person in San Francisco. We're open to sponsoring truly exceptional candidates on a case-by-case basis, but our main scope will be candidates who don't require this.

responsibilities: About e3Group e3 Group is a San Francisco AI company rebuilding freight brokerage around autonomous agents. We put voice and email negotiation, load matching, document processing, fraud detection, and legacy-system modernization into production for real brokerages — the unglamorous, high-stakes workflows that move freight and money every day. We're small, founder-led, and shipping fast: our agents do real work in front of paying customers, where a wrong number or a dropped call has consequences. About the Role We're hiring full-stack engineers who can build production AI end-to-end and own it. This isn't a feature factory — you'll take a problem from the first customer call through the product decision, the code, the deploy, and the traces you watch afterward, then do it again the next week. The surface is real full-stack (React, Next.js, Python), but the center of gravity is applied AI: LLM-driven voice and email agents, streaming speech pipelines, tool-calling with hard guardrails, retrieval, and the evals that keep any of it trustworthy. It's a high bar, and we'd rather be upfront about how we actually evaluate people — because it's exactly how we run interviews: We go straight at the biggest claim on your resume. Tell us what you personally built, how it works under the hood, how you measured whether it was right, what broke, and what you changed. "My team did that" is fine — as long as you're clear about your part. Evaluation is non-negotiable. If your answer to "how did you know this was correct before any user told you?" is spot-checks or a good prompt, that's a flag. Golden sets, regression and hallucination checks, and tool-call correctness are the language we want. Voice and agents are the domain: streaming, barge-in, latency budgets, and deterministic checks around anything an LLM can get wrong — prices, terms, actions. Think from first principles. Reason about scale, cost, and context limits from scratch; reach for embeddings, retrieval, and reranking before brute force. Work like an AI-native engineer. Claude Code and Codex are daily tools, and you can verify what they produce instead of trusting it blindly. We're not chasing perfect. Some of our best hires needed a nudge on hard problems — what mattered was getting to the right answer, reasoning honestly, and owning their thinking. What You'll Own Own features end-to-end and ship them weekly: scope the problem with a customer, build across the stack, deploy, and watch the production traces yourself. Build the voice and email negotiation agents — the speech pipeline (STT, TTS, turn-taking), the LLM orchestration, and the deterministic rules that keep prices and terms correct. Build the evaluation layer: golden datasets, offline and online checks, regression and hallucination testing, and tool-call correctness for everything the agents do. Build retrieval and matching on embeddings and reranking, tuned for cost and latency at real scale. Instrument production observability for three audiences at once: engineers debugging, product verifying correctness, and customers who need to trust the outcome. Bring product judgment — tell the difference between a one-off customer request and a real signal worth building around. Must-Have 5+ years shipping production software with real end-to-end ownership across a full stack (Python and TypeScript/React). Hands-on experience taking LLM features to production — architecture, tool-calling, and retrieval, not just prompting. Fluency with evaluation and testing for AI systems: how you know something works before a user tells you it doesn't. Strong system-design fundamentals — streaming, concurrency, SQL, and reasoning about scale and cost from first principles. Comfort with ambiguity and high-stakes calls on limited data, plus generative AI tooling (Claude Code, Codex) as daily instruments you direct and verify. Nice-to-Have Voice or real-time systems experience: STT/TTS, barge-in, latency budgets, telephony. Founding or early-stage engineer background — evidence you can operate without a playbook. Functional languages (OCaml, Haskell, Scala, Rust) or hardware description languages as a signal of depth and range. Multi-agent orchestration, negotiation flows, or other complex tool-use systems. Open-source work or personal projects shipping at scale; competitive programming as a supplementary signal.

  • We go straight at the biggest claim on your resume. Tell us what you personally built, how it works under the hood, how you measured whether it was right, what broke, and what you changed. "My team did that" is fine — as long as you're clear about your part.

  • Evaluation is non-negotiable. If your answer to "how did you know this was correct before any user told you?" is spot-checks or a good prompt, that's a flag. Golden sets, regression and hallucination checks, and tool-call correctness are the language we want.

About Mem0
Mem0 is building the memory layer for AI agents. Long-term memory that enables AI to remember conversations, learn from interactions, and build context over time. Already powering millions of AI interactions. YC-backed, $24M Series A raised with a team of four, based in San Francisco and well capitalized. 50K+ github stars, 25M python package downloads.

Our Culture

Office-first in San Francisco. Hallway chats, impromptu whiteboard sessions, and shared meals spark ideas that remote calls cannot. We build for the long term, not just shipping features. We move fast but never sacrifice reliability or thoughtful design. Every system needs to be fast, reliable, and elegant.

Everyone at Mem0 is a builder-owner. If you spot a problem or opportunity, you have the agency to fix it. Titles are light, impact is heavy. The best solution wins, whether it comes from a founder or an engineer who joined yesterday.

About the Role

Mem0 is hiring a Backend Engineer to own the backend that powers Mem0's memory platform. You will design clean REST APIs, model data across relational and graph stores, and operate services in production. When customers hit issues, you will chase them down to the root cause, ship fixes, and harden the system, while collaborating closely with the frontend and research teams to deliver fast, reliable features.

This is one of the first two engineering hires in SF, reporting directly to the founders. You are not a supporting engineer on an existing team. You are setting the standard.

Key Responsibilities

  • Design and ship REST APIs: define contracts, versioning, auth, rate limits, write migrations, and docs

  • Model data and schemas across relational (PostgreSQL) and graph (Neo4j or equivalent) stores, enforce integrity and performance

  • Debug customer issues end-to-end: trace with logs, metrics, and traces, reproduce, fix, and write preventative guardrails

  • Optimize performance: tune slow SQL with EXPLAIN and ANALYZE, indexes, partitioning, pagination, and caching (Redis)

  • Build services in Python: async, where it helps (FastAPI, Starlette, Django, DRF, Flask), background jobs, queues, and schedulers

  • Operate in the cloud: containerize with Docker, deploy on Kubernetes (EKS), and use AWS primitives (EC2, RDS, Aurora, S3, IAM)

  • Instrument everything: custom metrics, structured logging, tracing, set SLOs and alerts (CloudWatch, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry)

  • Collaborate with frontend and research to scope APIs and deliver features to production

Requirements

Must-Have

  • 5 to 8 years building backend systems and shipping REST APIs to production

  • Strong Python fundamentals with experience in async programming and a major web framework (FastAPI, Django, or Flask)

  • Solid data modeling and SQL skills, hands-on with query tuning and performance debugging in PostgreSQL or MySQL

  • Experience with graph databases (Neo4j or Amazon Neptune) and appropriate data modeling trade-offs

  • Comfortable running services on AWS with Docker and Kubernetes

  • Demonstrated root-cause analysis and ownership from incident to prevention

  • Clear communicator and effective collaborator with frontend, research, and customers

  • Based in or willing to relocate to San Francisco, fully in-person, 5 to 6 days a week

Nice-to-Have

  • GraphQL or gRPC, event-driven systems (SNS, SQS, Kafka), and background workers (Celery, RQ)

  • Caching, rate limiting, multi-tenancy, and feature-flag strategies

  • Security and privacy best practices: PII handling, secrets management

  • Deep observability experience: OpenTelemetry, SLO-based alerting

  • Prior work with search, retrieval, or memory systems

  • On-call experience and running blameless postmortems

About the Company

Bespoke Labs is a VC-backed applied AI research startup based in Mountain View, California, that builds core infrastructure and reinforcement learning environments to directly train and evaluate intelligent agents. Their work includes OpenThoughts, one of the most widely used open reasoning datasets with 100K+ monthly downloads, 200+ models trained, and 100+ citations, and Terminal Bench, a leading agentic coding benchmark referenced in Claude 4.5 and actively used by frontier AI labs. Founded by ex-Google DeepMind and UC Berkeley faculty, with advisors including Jeff Dean.

About the Role

Bespoke Labs is launching a new AI training initiative that requires real-world senior engineering experience. You will design and document authentic DevOps and backend engineering scenarios based on incidents you have personally handled, converting real-world outages, scaling challenges, secure deployments, and distributed systems problems into benchmark tasks that directly train next-generation AI systems.

The quality of AI training data depends on the authenticity and depth of the engineering scenarios behind it. Bespoke needs senior engineers with genuine hands-on experience to generate the kinds of complex, realistic scenarios that frontier labs cannot synthesize on their own.

Fully remote, flexible pacing, output-based compensation model. You earn based on completed deliverables, not tracked hours. High-performing contributors complete multiple outputs per week. Clear acceptance criteria are provided upfront for every deliverable.

What You'll Own

  • Work across backend services, including Go, Python, Docker, gRPC, and Kubernetes-native tooling

  • Capture real DevOps and backend engineering incidents and convert them into benchmark tasks with clear documentation

  • Contribute to secure, scalable, Kubernetes-native architectures across CI/CD, observability, identity, and infrastructure-as-code

  • Collaborate with the Bespoke team to build realistic, high-quality engineering workflows for AI training

  • Deliver approved engineering outputs on a flexible but consistent cadence across the 3-month contract

Requirements

Must-Have

Technical Foundation

  • 2 to 15 years of experience in backend engineering, with strong DevOps and infrastructure knowledge

  • Technical degree in CS, Engineering, or equivalent

  • Proven experience building, deploying, and operating backend services in production environments

  • Deep expertise in Kubernetes, Terraform, and CI/CD pipelines

  • Proficiency in Go, Python, or Java with Docker, gRPC, and Kubernetes-native services

  • Hands-on experience with at least five of the following: Identity and Access Management, Observability (Prometheus and Grafana), CI/CD Pipelines, Keycloak, GitLab CI, Terraform OSS, Kubernetes tools and ecosystem

Execution and Ownership

  • Ability to work independently and deliver high-quality outputs without close supervision

  • Comfortable with a flexible, output-based work structure

  • Strong written communication in English for documentation and scenario capture

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience with secure, offline, or air-gapped deployments, this is a strong plus

  • ML pipeline or distributed systems experience

  • Prior AI training data or benchmarking experience is not required, but a bonus

  • GitLab CI is preferred over other CI/CD tools

Who Will Thrive Here

Someone who:

  • Has built and operated real backend systems at scale and has the incident stories to prove it

  • Enjoys translating hands-on engineering experience into clear, structured documentation

  • Wants flexible, remote contract work with transparent earning potential

  • Is comfortable working autonomously with clear deliverable criteria

Location / Work Model

Fully remote, anywhere in the world. Contract position, approximately 3 months, 30 to 40 hours per week. Preferred 1099 independent contractor for US-based applicants, no H-1B sponsorship or visa support available

Compensation and Benefits

Output-based model: $600 to $1,000 per approved engineering deliverable. Each deliverable typically requires 12 to 20 hours of focused engineering work. Expected total compensation over contract lifespan: $10,000 to $50,000, depending on output volume and quality. Flexible pacing, optimize your own workflow, and earn potential. Recruiter bounty: 20% of total contract compensation

Hiring Process

  1. Take-home assignment

  2. Offer

responsibilitiesHtml:
About Simula

Simula is an a16z-backed AI ad network building the monetization layer for AI companion platforms. We've reached 30M+ unique users across our partner network by creating AI-native advertising formats that integrate seamlessly into AI chat experiences.

We are building a production-grade React Native Ad SDK powered by native Swift (iOS) and Kotlin (Android) layers underneath to power ad delivery, attribution, and privacy compliance across our publisher network.

The Role

We are hiring a Mobile SDK Contractor for an estimated 100 hour engagement over 1 2 months. The architecture is native-first: you will write the core ad logic in Swift (iOS) and Kotlin (Android), then bridge both into a unified React Native package that publishers consume.

You will own:

  • Writing core ad logic natively in Swift (iOS) and Kotlin (Android)

  • Bridging both native layers into a clean, unified React Native package

  • Ensuring correct ad display, low latency, and accurate attribution

  • Working with Simula's backend team to debug delivery and tracking issues

  • Implementing privacy compliance (ATT, consent signals)

This engagement starts as a focused contract, but for the right person it has a clear path forward. If the collaboration goes well, we are open to a longer-term or full-time role, as well as additional SDK projects across Flutter and React Native.

What You'll Build

1. Native Layers: Swift (iOS) + Kotlin (Android)

  • Implement core ad lifecycle handling (request, render, impression, click) natively in Swift and Kotlin

  • Build support for two ad formats:

    • Rewarded Ads: Full-screen opt-in ad unit with completion tracking and server-side reward verification callbacks

    • Interstitial Ads: Full-screen ads at natural transition points, with configurable close button delay and smooth enter/exit animations

  • Ensure correct rendering, low-latency display, and thread safety (main-thread UI operations)

  • Handle WebView-based creatives where applicable, manage WebView lifecycle, impression tracking, and click handling

2. React Native Bridge

  • Bridge the native Swift and Kotlin modules into a single, unified React Native package

  • Implement using React Native's native module system (not Expo-specific)

  • Expose a clean API surface supporting: SDK initialization, ad loading, ad display, event callbacks (load, impression, click, reward, close, error), and privacy configuration

  • Publishers should be able to integrate and display their first ad in under 30 minutes

3. Attribution & Store Redirect

  • Correctly open App Store (iOS) and Google Play (Android) download pages when a user clicks an ad

  • Pass the correct attribution parameters through the click URL so downstream attribution (AppsFlyer, Adjust, or direct) can fire accurately

  • Implement click deduplication and ensure no double-firing of click events

  • Work with Simula's backend team to validate that attribution signals are reaching the right endpoints

4. Privacy & Consent Compliance

  • Respect App Tracking Transparency (ATT) status on iOS 14.5+ and degrade gracefully when tracking is denied

  • Read and respect consent signals from SharedPreferences (Android) / NSUserDefaults (iOS) where available

  • Support a COPPA flag for child-directed content and strip identifiers when set

  • Expose a simple Privacy Configuration API for publishers to pass consent status and opt-out signals

5. Backend Debugging & Signal Integrity

  • Actively collaborate with Simula's backend team to debug ad delivery, impression discrepancies, and attribution mismatches

  • Instrument the SDK with sufficient logging to diagnose edge cases (failed loads, missed impressions, click-but-no-redirect scenarios)

  • Validate that all signals, impressions, clicks, completions, rewards, are reaching the backend correctly before handoff

Deliverables

  • Native iOS module (Swift) and Android module (Kotlin)

  • React Native bridge package (publishable to npm)

  • Sample React Native app demonstrating Rewarded and Interstitial ad formats

  • Publisher integration guide and API reference

Truvo's team is comprised of founding engineers with elite technical backgrounds, including published research and top accelerator programs, as well as a Director of Sales recruited from one of the top three digital insurance brokers in the country, who is bringing their top sales talent along.

About the Role

This is a high-leverage generalist role sitting directly next to the CEO, Charles. The Chief of Staff owns whatever is most important that week, whether that is fundraising, operations, GTM, analytics, partnerships, or product strategy. The scope is intentionally broad and constantly changing.

About AfterQuery

AfterQuery builds the training data and evaluation infrastructure that frontier AI labs use to improve their models. We work with the world's leading labs to design high signal datasets and run rigorous evaluations that go beyond static benchmarks. We are a small, early team (post Series A) where individual contributors have a direct impact on how the next generation of models learns and improves.

The Role

As a SWE (Environments), you will design the datasets and evaluation rubrics that directly influence how frontier models learn. You'll work hands-on with research teams at top AI labs, experimenting with data-collection strategies, diagnosing model failure modes, and developing metrics to determine whether a model is actually improving. You'll go from hypothesis to live experiment quickly, and your output will feed directly into model training runs at scale.

Day to day, you will design data slices that expose meaningful failure modes across domains like finance, code, and enterprise workflows. You will build and refine reward signals for RLHF and RLVR pipelines. You will develop quantitative frameworks for measuring dataset quality, diversity, and downstream impact on alignment and capability. You will partner with lab research teams to translate their training objectives into concrete data and evaluation specifications.

Compensation is $200K base plus profit share of roughly 150% of base, bringing expected total cash to around $500K, plus competitive equity.

What You'll Do

  • Design data slices and explore data shapes that expose meaningful model failure modes across domains like finance, code, and enterprise workflows

  • Build and refine evaluation rubrics and reward signals for RLHF and RLVR training pipelines

  • Model annotator behavior and run experiments to improve different model capabilities

  • Develop quantitative frameworks for measuring dataset quality, diversity, and downstream impact on model alignment and capability

  • Create and manage both real-world and synthetic data pipelines

  • Partner with lab research teams to translate their training objectives into concrete data and evaluation specifications

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 1–4 years of software engineering experience with strong technical depth

  2. Genuine obsession with how data structure, selection, and quality drive model behavior

  3. Ability to design lightweight experiments, move fast, and extract actionable insights from messy results

  4. Comfort working across domains, finance, software engineering, policy, and more

  5. Track record of shipping, bias toward building, not theorizing

Nice-to-Have

  • Prior work or internship at an RL environment company, AI safety org, or benchmarking org (METR, Artificial Analysis, or equivalent)

  • Former founder or early engineer at an early-stage startup

  • Experience building data pipelines (real-world + synthetic)

  • Familiarity with RLHF / RLVR training pipelines

Hundreds of teams building autonomous agents rely on Judgment to understand how their systems are behaving post-deployment. About the Role:

Judgment Labs is hiring an Agent Product Engineer to build high-taste products for self-learning agents. This role is crucial for scaling the product to meet customer demand and maintaining a reputation for exceptional user experience in the rapidly evolving AI agent space. The right person is passionate about improving agent behavior and can contribute to a product that is both powerful and a joy to use. The role is majority agent work with a baseline of full-stack engineering required. Candidates can come from a front-end/design engineering background or an AI engineering background, but both must have prior experience building and designing agents, preferably at a startup with 0-1 product ownership.

Must-Have

About Loyd

loyd is building agents (not the slow kind) for the global entertainment industry and creator economy. Professionals at WME, UTA, Netflix, Night, and Live Nation use loyd today through its private beta.

loyd has a massive trust moat: AvA, a 270K+ proprietary distribution network of verified entertainment professionals. Led by Vince Morales (2x founder, UTA Ventures, Elevate Ventures), Warner Bailey (2x founder, WME, Live Nation), and Ryan McCaffrey (WMG, Hebbia AI, Robinhood), with technical talent from NVIDIA, Intuit, and HubSpot. Advisors from CAA, UTA, Meta, Promise, Magic Leap, and Patreon. They have thousands on their waitlist and active beta users from all talent agencies.

The company oversubscribed its last $400K round through angels from Coatue, Ramp, Plug and Play, FanFix, Temple Hill, Outshine Talent, and Undercurrent Talent. Now raising $2M with +$500K already committed.

About the Role

Loyd is hiring an Applied AI Engineer dedicated to agent reliability. The mandate is deliberately narrow. The team does not need another full-stack engineer or a generic senior architect. They need someone whose hands stay in the eval pipeline and who turns the multi-agent system from "works in demos" into "survives non-deterministic LLM output at production scale." You will partner with our technical co-founder on architecture decisions where reliability is at stake, including HITL escalation, thread context collapse, and multi-channel routing. Our team owns the long-term evals vision, with additional support migrating in over the summer. This hire builds and runs the pipeline day-to-day.

What You'll Own

  • Instrument the scheduling agent end-to-end with traces on top of the existing Langfuse deployment

  • Build eval datasets from real production traffic across the agent layer (scheduling, notetaker, iMessage, Gmail)

  • Stand up the Braintrust scoring pipeline, including both quality scorers and robustness scorers (did the system survive the LLM output, did HITL trigger when it should)

  • Own the feedback loop from evals to prompt and architecture changes to re-evaluation, including DSPy and DPO as the system matures

  • Partner with the technical co-founder on agent architecture decisions where reliability is at stake

  • Operate end-to-end on your workstream: dev, test, deploy, and on-call sustain

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. Real production experience with non-deterministic LLM systems. Evidence of shipping, debugging, and maintaining agent systems under real traffic. Not side projects or OpenAI API experimentation.

  2. Has built or operated an eval pipeline before. If not Braintrust specifically, the intuition for scorer design has to be there.

  3. Product-first mindset applied to evals. Can take a scorer design and feedback loops and drive a real product forward, not just build models in isolation.

  4. Strong Python backend fluency. The stack is FastAPI, Django, Celery, and LangGraph, the hire ships on that stack.

  5. Comfortable with observability tooling (Langfuse or equivalent) and logs/metrics stacks like Grafana or Loki.

  6. Senior enough to own a workstream end-to-end from dev to test to deploy to on-call sustain. No pair programming crutch.

  7. Works async, writes clearly, fluent English.

Nice-to-Have

  • DSPy, DPO, or other LLM optimization experience

  • Prior agentic systems work with LangGraph or similar (tool use, planning, multi-step)

  • Time at a prestige-tier LATAM company (Nubank, Itaú, iFood) or a strong YC/US startup

  • Exposure to multi-model stacks (GPT-4.1/4o, Claude, Whisper) in production

About the Role Wispr Flow is making it as effortless to interact with your devices as talking to a close friend. Today, Wispr Flow is the first voice-dictation platform people use more than their keyboards, because it understands them perfectly on the first try. It's context-aware, personalized, and works anywhere you can type, on desktop or phone. In 2026, in addition to dictation, the team is focused on building native actions, an agentic framework that understands you and works reliably. Wispr Flow is a team of AI researchers, designers, growth experts, and engineers rethinking human-computer interaction from the ground up. The team values high-agency teammates who communicate openly, obsess over users, and sweat the details. About the Role Flow on iOS is an AI keyboard that lives inside every app on your phone, including Slack, Gmail, and Notion. A keystroke that works perfectly in Notes might break in a custom rich text editor after a permission revoke, specifically on iOS 26.4. Catching those breaks before users do is a full-time engineering problem, and Wispr Flow is hiring a Senior SDET to own it. This is a hybrid engineering and quality role. You will write Swift, build XCUITest infrastructure that runs on every PR, and own the automated systems that protect text insertion, permission flows, and keyboard extension behavior across Wispr's host app matrix. The team is looking for someone with a deep background in iOS engineering who has chosen to focus on quality. You have shipped iOS code, you understand the keyboard extension lifecycle and its memory limits, and you write test code that other engineers depend on. If you have high ownership, an obsessive eye for detail, and want to build the safety net that lets Wispr ship Flow on iOS confidently every week, this role is for you. What You'll Do Own iOS test automation end-to-end. Design and maintain XCUITest suites that verify text insertion, keyboard activation, onboarding, and permission flows on every PR. When a build is green, engineers should trust it. Test Flow inside other apps. Use Maestro, Appium, or whatever tool fits to drive real host apps and confirm that Flow behaves correctly across UITextField, UITextView, WKWebView, and custom inputs. Hunt edge cases in permissions and extension lifecycle. Full Access toggles, mic grants and revokes, iOS upgrades, and memory pressure killing the keyboard mid-session. Write tests that catch regressions in the exact spots where iOS bites. Read code to test smarter. Look at diffs to understand a change's blast radius. If a PR touches audio session handling, stress-test interruption from incoming calls, Bluetooth switching, and long dictation sessions. Use AI tools to debug and investigate. Use Claude Code and similar tools to trace through the codebase and narrow down root causes. Bug reports include precise context: code path, device/OS combo, Instruments traces, recordings, and the commit SHA. Engineers can reproduce from your report alone. Profile performance and battery. Catch the memory leak, the CPU spike, the battery regression in CI before it ships. Requirements Must-Have 5+ years of iOS engineering or SDET experience on native iOS apps Strong Swift skills and ability to write production-quality test code Deep XCUITest experience plus familiarity with at least one cross-platform tool (Maestro preferred) Hands-on experience testing keyboard extensions, share extensions, or other iOS app extensions Solid grasp of iOS permissions, entitlements, sandboxing, and extension memory limits Familiarity with AI-assisted development tools (Claude Code, Cursor, or similar) Meticulous bug reporting: reproduction steps, logs, recordings, device/OS details, commit references High ownership mindset, treats shipped bugs as personal failures Nice-to-Have Experience testing voice, audio, or ML-powered products Familiarity with accessibility testing and assistive technology Experience with crash reporting and analytics tools (Sentry, PostHog, or similar) Prior work on apps that integrate at the OS level (keyboards, share extensions, Lock Screen widgets, Siri shortcuts)

Please click here to read Conversion's Growth Marketing Hiring Brief for critical info before sourcing for this role.

About Conversion

Conversion is the AI-native marketing automation platform for modern software companies. Our platform lets growth teams run their entire go-to-market motion in one place, from acquisition through retention, with AI agents doing the work that legacy tools like Marketo, HubSpot, and Pardot can't.

We've raised $28M+ from Abstract Ventures, True Ventures, and HOF Capital. The team is based in San Francisco and includes engineers, designers, and operators from Airbnb, Palantir, Pinterest, IMC, Shopify, LinkedIn, and Microsoft.

About the Role

Hey! 👋 Kyle here. I run product and growth at Conversion. This role has been genuinely hard to put into words because it's ambiguous, fast-moving, and deeply creative. Bear with me.

We're in a really lucky spot right now. We have a product people are excited about. We have a sales team ready to sell it. We have specialists and partners across demand gen, paid, and the broader marketing ops world. The thing we need to move faster next? A creative.

I've heard this role called everything from "PMM" to "storyteller" to "that person who just makes everything look and feel better." At its core, it's someone with a strong vision for brand and creative, who's savvy with creative tools, and who has an almost annoying attention to detail.

Now here's the tricky part. I've been trying to help our hiring team nail down what the right candidate looks like, and honestly... there's no clean checklist. You don't need B2B SaaS experience. You don't need a marketing degree. Some of the best people for this kind of role come from design backgrounds, community backgrounds, content backgrounds, or something totally different. So instead of listing requirements, here's what I've noticed is actually true about the people who crush it in roles like this:

  1. They love to share work and own brand. They have side projects. Maybe an app, an art Instagram, a little vlog series from their last trip. They just naturally make things and put them out into the world.

  2. They're drawn to advertising and creative work. They have opinions about campaigns. (I maintain a tier list for Super Bowl ads, so no judgment here.)

  3. They're obsessed with details and craft. If they host a dinner party, they design a cute menu to hand out. They're the friend who gives an unbelievably thoughtful Secret Santa gift. They have a Notion doc to organize the group trip. You know the type.

Responsibilities

  • Work on exciting new product launches: launch videos, webpages, and collateral

  • Help build out ambitious end-to-end creative programs, like starting Conversion Academy

  • Work with partners and influencers to represent and grow the brand

  • Ideate and execute growth experiments across new channels

  • Own end-to-end content creation: concept, script, shoot, edit, publish

  • Turn features, workflows, and real customer use cases into relatable, compelling content

  • Design and produce events and programming: hack nights, speaker series, tactical sessions, dinners

  • Build and nurture community through onboarding experiences, meetups, and digital channels

  • Build lightweight systems to keep programs organized (Airtable, calendars, speaker tracking, etc.)

  • Rigorously track performance and iterate quickly based on what's working

This role is in-person 5 days/week in San Francisco.

You Might Be a Good Fit If You

  • Have a knack for storytelling and turning the mundane into something people actually want to watch or read

  • Are relentless about experimenting with hooks, formats, trends, and narrative styles to build repeatable content that compounds over time

  • Have strong organizational skills and can manage multiple initiatives in a fast-paced environment

  • Are comfortable with outreach through social media and digital channels

  • Have impeccable attention to detail, aesthetic sensibility, and craft

  • Are highly collaborative and can work across product, engineering, sales, and design

  • Thrive in a startup environment where you have real ownership and autonomy

You Might Be a Great Fit If You

  • You believe in high-intensity, in-person teams and want to be surrounded by top talent pushing in the same direction

  • You have the range to shift from editing a launch video to planning a community dinner to writing ad copy without skipping a beat

  • You care deeply about your craft: every email, every thumbnail, every slide

  • You live and breathe content, trends, and algorithms

  • You have experience with the startup ecosystem and understand what makes early-stage companies tick

Useful Links

  • Website: https://conversion.ai/

  • Learn more about our company culture here: https://conversion.ai/careers

About the company

Tldr on us: Series B, $91M raised, 7x growth last year.

Digital Transformation gave rise to a $600B consulting Industry. AI Transformation will be 10x bigger and will be delivered through agents. We built that.

Our AI discovers how work actually happens across every team and application, Structures it into a living Context Graph, and improves it continuously.

ServiceNow mapped 900+ processes in 9 days. DoorDash captured 3,800+ finance operations in 14 weeks. That's not a project. That's compounding intelligence.

OpenAI, Google, DoorDash, and Stripe use Within to transform how they transform. We shipped GPT-4 document chat within 12 hours of OpenAI's API launch.

We move fast, reward agency, and care deeply about our customers, our team, and our mission.

About the Role

Within (formerly Klarity) is hiring a Staff AI Frontend Engineer who sits at the intersection of product design and frontend engineering. You are an engineer first, but with exceptional design sensibility that elevates everything you build. You will define and implement the look and feel of AI-native workflows, ensuring complex enterprise tools feel as intuitive as the best consumer apps. The product includes a real-time,e WebRTC-powered companion agent that follows users across their screen, generative dashboards that visualize complex enterprise context graphs, agentic chat that operates the web application directly, and a fundamentally new UI paradigm built around generative AI. You will ship at AI speeds, work directly with a tight founding team, and help define the future of frontend SDLC.

What You'll Own

  • Architect scalable frontend systems: design reusable component libraries, establish patterns for state management and API integration, optimize bundle sizes, ensure the platform performs beautifully at scale

  • Own and ship the primary user-facing features users interact with daily, end-to-end from React components through API integration to production polish

  • Bridge AI capabilities with elegant user experiences: partner with product and backend engineers to expose powerful functionality while hiding technical complexity

  • Build complex frontend systems, including real-time WebRTC streaming for the companion agent, generative dashboards, and agentic chat that operates the product itself

  • Use AI tools to rapidly prototype design concepts in code, bridging gaps between teams with working demos instead of static mocks

  • Help define how the team scales code review and SDLC with agents that encode your architectural thinking

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 6+ years shipping production-grade products. Senior to Staff level.

  2. Mastery of modern web technologies: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind. You understand the performance consequences of architectural decisions and ship code that's elegant and performant.

  3. AI-native developer. You wield Cursor, Claude Code, v0.dev, Lovable, and comparable tools as extensions of your craft. You ship multiple features per day with AI assistance.

  4. Engineer first, designer by instinct. You discuss Server vs Client Components as fluently as you critique spacing and visual hierarchy.

  5. High agency. You've pushed yourself outside structured environments as a founder, founding engineer, or with significant scope ownership at a real startup.

  6. On the bleeding edge of AI tooling. You can articulate what changed in your stack in the last three months.

  7. Comfortable talking to customers and sales. You shape product through action, not waiting for permission.

  8. Based in SF or willing to relocate immediately. In-person 5 days a week downtown SF.

Nice-to-Have

  • Prior founder or founding engineer experience

  • Real-time WebRTC streaming or video pipeline experience

  • Voice AI product experience

  • Generative UI or generative dashboard work

  • Python backend comfort for occasional cross-stack work

  • No CS or Engineering degree required; portfolio, GitHub, and shipping track record matter more

Klarity provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, or veteran status.

About Warp

Warp is building self-driving employee management, payroll, tax compliance across thousands of jurisdictions, benefits, IT, and HRIS that runs autonomously, so companies never have to think about back-office operations again. The team processes hundreds of millions in payments across 1,000+ companies. Revenue has grown 5x+ YoY for two years and is currently growing 20%+ month over month, putting Warp in the top 5% of startups by growth.

The incumbents (ADP, Paylocity, Paychex) built their businesses by profiting from complexity. Even the modern players are bolting chatbots onto legacy systems. Warp is built from day one to make AI the primary operator, not a feature. Every advance in LLM capability widens the lead. The team is ~40 people in NYC Flatiron, scaling to 100 by the end of the year.

Warp is the only company in the market that is not a PEO and provides full liability and end-to-end payroll compliance — including state registrations, tax filings, and tax notices. There is no direct competitor doing this today. Any U.S. company with an EIN is fair game, so the TAM is unlimited.

Backed by $25M+ from Ashton Kutcher / Sound Ventures, Y Combinator, the founders of Dropbox, Replit, SV Angel, and Homebrew Capital. Built by an obsessive team from MIT, Ramp, Brex, Google, Dropbox, and Apple.

About The Role

Warp is hiring Account Executives to run full-cycle sales — from outbound prospecting through demo, close, and handoff to customer success. You will own a $70K monthly ARR quota and self-source 40% of your pipeline. The other 60% comes from SDR-sourced outbound, inbound, and partner channels. The product is differentiated, the TAM is unlimited (any U.S. company with an EIN), and the accelerators are aggressive, with a 2x commission rate at 140% attainment.

This is the right seat for closers who want unlimited ceiling, are hungry to make money, and can operate independently in a fast-moving startup environment. The AE who closed Warp's largest seat deal last month brought in $1.2M ARR on a $70K monthly quota. There is no segment lock; you can sell to gas stations or to enterprises. Reps who hit quota typically work around 9 hours a day. 5 of 6 current AEs are at or above quota.

What You'll Own

  • Run full-cycle sales: outbound prospecting → discovery → demo → close → handoff to customer success

  • Self-source 30% of your pipeline through outbound. Non-negotiable structural requirement.

  • Hit a $70K monthly ARR quota with accelerators above target (1.25x at 100-120%, 1.5x at 120-140%, 2x above 140%)

  • Build your own decks and figure things out. The team does not have a sales engineer, and Warp is still a startup with processes that flex weekly

  • Maintain and log all sales touchpoints in CRM

  • Collaborate with SDRs, marketing, and product to create a smooth buying experience. You will be matched 1:1 with an SDR

  • Travel only if you want to, not a requirement of the role

Requirements

Must-Have

8+ months of full-cycle closing experience. Sweet spot 2-3 years. Cap around 5 years.

Comfort self-sourcing 30% of your own pipeline through outbound. Non-negotiable.

Hungry to make money. The accelerators only matter if you push past 100% attainment.

Independent operator who builds decks, figures out CRM, and adapts without process or sales engineering support.

Strong written and verbal communication. Comfort moving fast through full cycles.

Based in NYC or willing to relocate. 5 days in the office in Flatiron.

Top 5% performer at current or recent company. The current AE bench was hired on this signal.

Must have been an Business/Sales Development Representative in the past (outbound role)

Nice-to-Have

Fast sales cycle background

Payroll, compliance, fintech, or HR tech product experience

Startup sales experience (Series A-C)

Experience selling SMB through enterprise without segment lock

Compensation & Benefits

Base: $100,000 - $130,000

OTE: $190,000 - $250,000
Candidates can choose 50/50 split or 70/30 split depending on the base desired

NOTE: Stem OPT transfers, but no new visas

Amari AI 

Global trade is a $10T industry still running on manual, document-heavy workflows. Customs brokerages spend hours per shipment on tasks that should take minutes. The companies fixing this are rare, and this is one of them.

This team builds AI agents that work alongside logistics teams to automate the operational tasks that slow every shipment. Their platform cuts customs clearance times to under 5 minutes and has already delivered 30,000+ hours back to brokerage teams. They have moved well past zero to one, with a strong MoM revenue growth, and customers processing meaningful operational volume every day.

$5M raised from First Round Capital and Pear VC. A deeply technical founding team from Google, LinkedIn, and Salesforce, with backgrounds from top schools and AI research labs.

The Role

As a Senior Backend Engineer at Amari, you will own the core data infrastructure powering their AI-driven logistics platform. This is a high-ownership, zero-to-one role; you'll design and scale the systems that ingest, process, and serve real-time logistics data across AI pipelines, queues, databases, and search layers. You'll set technical direction for the backend, operate with significant autonomy, and have an outsized impact on product reliability and performance from day one.

What You'll Do

  • Architect and scale distributed backend systems, design queue pipelines, communication hubs, and observability layers, and build for failure with retry strategies, circuit breakers, and graceful degradation

  • Own database design and reliability, schema design, indexing, query optimization, and data pipelines that keep systems in sync at scale

  • Build an AI search infrastructure for real-time logistics lookup and AI-driven features

  • Define service boundaries and set engineering standards for the backend

  • Collaborate directly with founders on roadmap and technical direction

  • Help hire and mentor future backend engineers as the team scales

Requirements
Must-Have

  1. 3 to 6 years of professional software engineering experience, strictly within this band

  2. Bachelor's degree from a reputable university

  3. Meaningful time in a high-growth startup or high-scale production environment

  4. Demonstrated ability to own and ship backend systems end-to-end in fast-moving, ambiguous environments

  5. Track record of making sound architectural trade-offs under time pressure and revisiting decisions as requirements evolve

  6. Real startup experience at a company of 10 or more people, not exclusively big tech

  7. Based in San Francisco or committed to relocating; fully in-person, non-negotiable

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience with distributed systems, message queues such as Kafka, RabbitMQ, or SQS, and event-driven architectures

  • Familiarity with AI or ML pipeline infrastructure or document processing at scale

  • Exposure to enterprise software requirements including security, data retention, privacy, and compliance

  • Experience with search infrastructure such as Elasticsearch or pgvector

  • Background at a high-growth Series A or B startup or as a founding engineer

  • Logistics, customs, or regulated industry software experience

This Role Is NOT For You If

  • You need large team structures, extensive documentation, or clearly defined quarterly roadmaps to be productive

  • You prefer isolated, single-component work with a narrowly bounded scope

  • Ambiguity and rapid pivots in early-stage startups are uncomfortable for you

Success Metrics

  • System Reliability: Core logistics services and queue-driven workflows maintain high uptime and low error rates under production load

  • Throughput & Latency: Message processing pipelines and search queries meet defined SLAs as data volumes grow

  • Architectural Quality: Backend systems are extensible, well-documented, and enable other engineers to build confidently on top of your foundations

  • Velocity: Scope, build, and ship new backend capabilities within sprint cycles without sacrificing correctness or resilience

  • Autonomy: Resolve complex technical blockers independently and surface the right issues at the right time

Why This Role

  • Doubled ARR within two months of closing their Series A

  • Direct mentorship from founders (ex-Google, ex-LinkedIn)

  • Full end-to-end ownership from day one, no tickets, no bureaucracy

  • Work on genuinely hard distributed systems problems at the intersection of AI and global trade

  • 30,000+ hours already returned to brokerage teams, the product works, now it needs to scale

  • Equity-first culture: 0.25 – 0.6%

About us

Sunset is one of the fastest-growing tech startups helping venture-backed companies shut down gracefully.
