About the Role

Sunset, experiencing ongoing growth, is expanding its Client Success team and is looking for a driven Client Success Manager based in New York City (or willing to relocate). The role reports to the Director of Client Success and has two main responsibilities: offering direct support to clients during the dissolution process and managing essential wind-down tasks, including filing dissolutions and redistributing capital to investors.

As a Client Success Manager at Sunset, you will own a dedicated set of clients through the entire lifecycle of a company shutdown. This is a hands-on role that blends direct client support with deep operational execution. Success is measured by speed, accuracy, and client confidence, not revenue, renewals, or upsell.

This role is a core part of Sunset's client success function, with a clear path to senior individual contributor or team leadership as the company scales.

What You'll Own

  • Be the first responder to all client queries across tickets, email, and phone for a dedicated set of accounts

responsibilitiesHtml:
About Tilde Research

Tilde focuses on building a mechanistic understanding of model architectures, optimizers, and their co-design, with the goal of enabling data-efficient reasoning models. Recent public work includes analyzing the rigidity of Manifold Muon to derive generalized manifolds for orthogonalized optimizers, and studying sparse attention to better understand how key–value parameterization shapes attention behavior. The team sees these results as early but concrete steps toward using mechanistic insight to guide new training methods. Ongoing work builds directly on this, as Tilde trains in-house model families for data-sparse regimes.

Tilde is the best of both worlds between academia and industry. The culture is genuinely curiosity-driven and first-principles, with people here because they care deeply about the science, but without the usual academic constraints. The team has strong funding, real compute, and the ability to move quickly. Tilde is very selective about capital and deliberately avoids investors who would push early commercialization. Everyone here is making a medium-term bet on where the field is actually headed.

About the Role

Tilde is hiring three ML Engineers to implement research ideas reliably and own end-to-end training work. The role pairs strong competence in PyTorch or JAX with transformer training, distributed setups, and evaluation. You will read research papers, turn them into working implementations, debug divergence, instability, and throughput bottlenecks at scale, and bring sufficient research intuition to reason about learning dynamics and optimization choices alongside the research team.

What You'll Own

  • Implement research ideas reliably in PyTorch or JAX, translating papers and internal proposals into production-grade code

  • Build and operate end-to-end training pipelines covering data, training, and evaluation

  • Run transformer training at scale across distributed setups

  • Debug training instability, divergence, and throughput bottlenecks

  • Reason about learning dynamics, optimization choices, and architecture-level tradeoffs alongside researchers

  • Read and implement custom architectures based on internal research direction

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. Strong PyTorch or JAX competence with the ability to implement research ideas reliably.

  2. Hands-on experience with transformer training, distributed setups, and evaluation frameworks.

  3. Comfort debugging large-scale training issues, including divergence, instability, and throughput bottlenecks.

  4. Ability to read research papers and implement custom architectures from them.

  5. Enough research intuition to reason about learning dynamics and optimization choices.

  6. High-slope operator. Open to new grads, dropouts, and senior engineers, the bar is rate of growth, not years.

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience with NVIDIA Megatron-LM, Nemotron, DeepSpeed, or xformers

  • Built end-to-end training pipelines covering data, training, and evaluation

  • Prior tenure at research-engineering teams: FAIR, DeepMind, Google Brain, OpenAI infra, MosaicML

  • Open-source contributions to PyTorch, Megatron, xformers, tinygrad, JAX repos, or comparable

  • Mathematical foundation in optimization, information theory, signal propagation, or learning dynamics

  • Competitive programming or theory-heavy academic background (IMO, IOI, CMU, MIT, Stanford, EPFL, HSE, DeepMind Scholars)

About DualEntry

Founded in 2024, DualEntry is one of the world's fastest-growing AI startups. ERP is one of the largest fintech markets in the world ($220B+ annually). Yet tens of thousands of companies are still running on-premise systems from the 1990s, and the industry has not seen new entrants in more than 30 years.

DualEntry's AI-native ERP lets accounting teams achieve more in less time. $5M-ARR businesses to NYSE-listed companies trust DualEntry to automate away manual data entry work with AI.

Since launching 18 months ago, DualEntry has raised $100M+ from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, Contrary Ventures, and Google Ventures, as well as 20+ angel investors. The team is from Ramp, Meta, Microsoft, Lyft, PwC, Deloitte, JP Morgan, Bloomberg, Sage, Xero, and Intuit.

About the Role

As VP of Sales, you will build and lead DualEntry's revenue engine. You will drive high-value deals, work closely with the founders, and help define how DualEntry sells as the company expands into multiple markets. This role is both hands-on and strategic: closing key deals while building and leading a high-performing sales team.

This is an intense, hands-on role with full ownership. The expectation is to push for excellence and raise the bar.

What You'll Own

  • Own the full sales motion from early discovery to signed contract

  • Lead complex sales cycles with CFOs and finance leaders

  • Hire, coach, and manage the sales team, building a culture of high standards, accountability, and continuous improvement

  • Work closely with founders, marketing, and product to refine messaging and shape how DualEntry sells

  • Help design the sales playbook and processes that support scalable growth

  • Build the outbound motion alongside the existing inbound-dominant pipeline


Requirements

Must-Have

  • Hardcore work ethic and high agency

  • 8+ years of experience in B2B SaaS sales

  • Experience leading and managing high-performing sales teams

  • Experience selling ERP, accounting, or financial systems to mid-market or enterprise companies

  • Comfortable selling to CFOs and finance leaders and managing multi-stakeholder sales cycles

  • Strong operator who can build sales structure, forecasting, and process

  • Hands-on player-coach who can both close deals and develop people

  • Prior 0-to-1 startup experience. Has grown a team and revenue at a startup, not just managed an existing function.

  • Track record of growing revenue from single digits to $15M-$25M+ ARR

  • Mid-market sales focus (not enterprise-only)

  • Based in NYC or commutable distance. 5 days a week at 7 World Trade Center.

Nice-to-Have

  • Strong preference for an accounting or audit background (CPA or Big 4 experience is a major plus per the founder)

  • Prior experience at a fintech selling into the office of the CFO

  • Prior experience transitioning a sales motion from 100% inbound to outbound + inbound

  • Prior experience building solutions, consulting, or BDR functions

Varick Agents is a San Francisco–based AI startup valued at $30M following a $3.8M seed round. About the Role

Varick is hiring Software Engineers to build the production agents that run inside enterprise operations at the largest companies on the planet. About the Company

The full platform, including the implementation, deploys directly into each client's environment, whether that's Varick's multi-tenant cloud, a dedicated instance, the client's VPC, on-prem, or fully air-gapped.

About the Role

The Engineering Lead runs Varick's engineering, leading the core platform team and the teams that deliver client implementations. The role partners with product owners to run multiple engagements simultaneously and owns the technical direction that determines whether Varick becomes a generational platform or remains a services business.

The Engineering Lead sets the technical bar, grows the team, and is accountable for what ships across every client, staying hands-on enough to make the hard calls and jump in where it counts as the company scales from 1:1 to 1:many. This role has a direct path to CTO.

What You'll Own

  • Lead the core platform team and multiple client-implementation teams, owning the seam between the platform and the implementations, and partner with product owners to run several engagements at once

  • Recruit, mentor, and grow engineers and future leads, setting code review and reliability standards and building an org that scales from 5 to 50

  • Set the architecture and technical bar across the platform and every implementation, make build-vs-buy calls, and translate developments in agent frameworks, tool use, and long-context reasoning into production

  • Guide the teams building compound agent systems, including multi-step orchestration, retrieval, structured extraction, evaluation suites, and confidence-gated human-in-the-loop, running inside enterprise ERP and CRM software

  • Own the multi-client fleet and infrastructure: per-client configuration and isolation across shared-cloud, dedicated, VPC, on-prem, and air-gapped deployments, fleet-wide upgrade and rollback, monitoring, alerting, and on-call, plus Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, and multi-cloud across AWS, GCP, and Azure

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 6+ years of software engineering, including real-time experience leading engineers as a lead, manager, or founding engineer accountable for a team's output

  2. Proven engineering leadership, having built, grown, and mentored engineering teams and owned delivery across multiple teams or workstreams at once

  3. Deep experience building and shipping AI agents in production, across orchestration, tool use, retrieval, structured extraction, evaluation, and human-in-the-loop, not just prompt demos

  4. Strong distributed-systems instincts, with depth in multi-tenant backend systems, data modeling, and enterprise integration, including real APIs, OAuth, connectors, and enterprise ERP and CRM software

  5. Comfortable owning infrastructure (Kubernetes, infrastructure-as-code, multi-cloud) and operating software across many deployments and versions, including release management, staged rollout, rollback, monitoring, alerting, and on-call

Nice-to-Have

  • Forward-deployed or customer-facing engineering experience, talking directly to the people whose process is being automated

  • Background in process mining, workflow automation, or enterprise process discovery

  • Previous founding engineer or CTO experience at a venture-backed startup

  • Experience operating in enterprise environments with real security, compliance, and reliability requirements (SOC 2, audit, on-call/incident response), or published research/open-source contributions in agents and applied AI

About DualEntry

DualEntry is building an AI-native ERP for modern finance teams. Founded in 2024, the company has raised over $100M from Lightspeed Venture Partners, Khosla Ventures, Contrary Ventures, Google Ventures, and more than 20 angels who've built and scaled impactful companies. DualEntry serves $5M-ARR businesses through NYSE-listed companies, automating manual data entry work and replacing legacy on-premise systems that haven't seen new entrants in over 30 years. The team grew to ~20+ people in 18 months, hiring from Ramp, Meta, Microsoft, Lyft, PwC, Deloitte, JP Morgan, Bloomberg, Sage, Xero, and Intuit.

About the Role

This is a high-ownership marketing leadership role reporting directly to the founding team (Ben and Santi). You'll own the marketing function end-to-end, scaling from a lean 7-person team across growth, product marketing, content, and video production into a multi-channel GTM engine. Your first 90 days focus on hiring, building repeatable processes, and defining channel prioritization; the next 6 months center on measurable pipeline contribution, operational rigor, and execution quality across the board. You'll work closely with the newly hired Head of Sales to align demand-generation and sales-enablement motions from day one.

What You'll Own

  • Own marketing end-to-end: strategy, positioning, messaging, brand, and multi-channel execution across content, paid, and website optimization

  • Build and scale the marketing organization: hire and mentor team leads for growth, product marketing, content, and paid channels

  • Drive consistent pipeline growth across key verticals by defining channel priorities, campaign strategy, and measurable KPIs

  • Establish operational rigor and playbooks: budget allocation frameworks, campaign processes, performance tracking, and funnel optimization

  • Partner directly with the Head of Sales to align demand-gen and sales-enablement motions, ensuring GTM cohesion from first touch through close

  • Lead brand positioning and competitive differentiation in a 30-year-old market seeing its first new entrant

Must-Have

  1. 6+ years senior marketing experience in high-growth startups, scaling through Series A to Series D phases

  2. Generalist marketing background with confidence in at least two domains (product marketing, demand generation, lifecycle, growth, brand) and ability to learn others

  3. Track record managing teams (at least 1-3 people at seed stage, or larger teams at later stage); team maturity matters more than team size

  4. Hands-on execution skills across multi-channel campaigns, content strategy, paid programs, and conversion optimization

  5. High agency and comfort with ambiguity; able to build processes and playbooks from scratch without a roadmap

  6. Experience selling into executive buyers (CFOs, finance leaders) and knowledge of the fintech or financial software market is a strong plus

  • Demonstrated ability to turn successful campaigns into repeatable systems and playbooks that scale

  • Each marketing function has a strong lead running it day to day.

  • Channel priorities are set, tested, and producing.

  • Positioning and messaging are locked and consistent across every surface (site, sales materials, campaigns).

  • Pipeline contribution is tracked, predictable, and trending up.

  • Budget, KPIs, and reporting cadences run on documented playbooks, not one-off efforts.

  • Campaigns ship on time and to a consistent quality bar.

responsibilitiesHtml:
About Black Ore

Black Ore is an AI platform for financial services. Its flagship product, Tax Autopilot, autonomously prepares tax returns for CPA and accounting firms.

The company launched to a waiting list of > 4,000 accounting firms after operating in stealth with 40% of the Top 20 CPA firms, delivering 99% accuracy and saving up to 98% of preparation time compared to manual workflows.

The company is rapidly accelerating toward $100M ARR and is backed by Oak HC/FT, a16z, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, Khosla Ventures, and Trust Ventures, along with notable angels including Tom Glocer (former CEO, Thomson Reuters), Max Levchin (founder, PayPal and Affirm), and Gokul Rajaram.

Our team has an incredibly ambitious vision to completely transform the way businesses and consumers interact in financial services. We’re looking to hire strong team members to grow the team. Some of the traits we look for are:

  • Owner Mentality - Desire to take initiative, identify problems, and implement solutions

  • Mission Driven - Passion for building AI/ML solutions that reimagine how businesses and consumers operate

  • Intellectually Curious - Excitement going deep for building a detailed understanding of the function, role, customer, and problem space

  • Team Oriented - Ability to collaborate respectfully and put the team above the self

About the Role

Black Ore is seeking Tax Technical Specialists to join the Information Architecture team and serve as tax domain experts for the design of an AI-native tax platform. You will collaborate with CPAs, architects, engineers, and AI engineers to deliver the next generation of AI-enabled innovation for financial services.

This role sits at the intersection of tax, information architecture, and AI-enabled technology design. You will spend significant time in Excel and Codex, writing technical requirements like a technical PM. You will translate complex tax concepts (high-net-worth 1040s, partnership K-1s, basis tracking) into a single source of truth: an opinionated data model that captures how tax actually works in the U.S., not just how the IRS happens to have codified it. You are the bridge between the tax brain and the engineering brain.

What You'll Own

  • Translate tax rules, regulatory guidance, and accounting concepts into structured data models, business rules, and computational logic

  • Research complex tax and regulatory guidance from authoritative sources to define requirements, taxonomies, rule sets, and integration workflows for tax automation

  • Build the canonical model: every form, every institution, every line item maps back to one consistent source of truth

  • Explain complex tax and accounting concepts to non-CPA technical stakeholders (architects, engineers, AI engineers)

  • QA system logic to ensure outputs match expected behavior (faulty logic, not hallucination, is the focus)

  • Use AI tools (Claude Code, Codex) daily to accelerate the delivery of models and implementation artifacts

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. CPA with 1.5+ years on the floor (minimum 2 tax seasons): experienced tax associate level or above, with end-to-end exposure to workpapers, review, and filing of 1040, 1065, and fiduciary returns

  2. High-net-worth tax depth: familiar with K-1s, partnerships, loss limitations, nonpassive activity classifications, grouping elections, and basis tracking. Pure C-Corp backgrounds do not clear.

  3. Beginner-or-better coding fluency: can read and write code in at least one language. Familiar with data structures (arrays, maps, linked lists), OOP concepts (classes, inheritance, encapsulation), and foreign keys.

  4. Can write algorithms explaining tax logic to non-CPAs and document workflows in diagram form

  5. AI-native: uses Claude Code, Codex, or comparable AI tooling daily as production tools, not just experimentally

Nice-to-Have

  • Background at boutique high-net-worth shops (Anderson, Centerbridge, comparable)

  • Previously transitioned from tax into automation, dev, or tech roles

  • Personally built workpapers, calculators, or tax automation tools

  • Familiarity with professional tax platforms (CCH Axcess, Thomson GoSystems, comparable)


Location: NYC primary, Austin secondary. Hybrid (come in when needed).

About Guthrie AI

Guthrie AI is building the AI-powered workflow layer for construction, one of the world's largest industries. Headquartered in Philadelphia with a remote-first team and a newly opened Philly hub. Just closed a seed round (term sheets signed, not yet announced), with ~$2M ARR on the core product and a plan to 10x in the next 12 months. The team includes a Chief AI Officer, seven engineers (two AI/ML, five full-stack), and a founding team operating the platform alongside customers.

Construction has resisted prior attempts at automation for over 15 years. Subcontractors, the company's core customer, have not seen meaningful software innovation in that time. Agents and multimodal AI are the first real wedge into an industry that skipped the software era. Off-the-shelf models from OpenAI and Anthropic struggle with construction diagrams since they're not represented in standard training data, which makes training in-house models a core technical bet.

About the Role

Guthrie is hiring a Founding AI / ML Engineer with deep computer vision expertise to own the model development side of the platform. Construction diagrams and floor plans are not in the training data of any off-the-shelf foundation model, which means Guthrie has to train its own. This role leads that work.

Half the role is computer vision (the irreplaceable part): segmentation models (SAM-tier work, ideally with 2D segmentation depth), classifiers, object detection on floor plans and technical drawings. Architectural and model improvements, not just fine-tuning. The other half is agentic orchestration and retrieval (LLM expertise, fine-tuning small language models, RAG, local vs foundation model trade-offs), which is important but where the team can survive with "good enough" if the CV expertise is exceptional.

Reports to the Chief AI Officer. The 2-3 existing AI/ML engineers will report to this person, so technical leadership and onsite presence for guidance are valued.

What You'll Own

  • Train and improve in-house computer vision models for construction diagrams (segmentation, object detection, classifiers)

  • Lead architectural and model-improvement work where off-the-shelf models hit their ceiling

  • Own the model development roadmap and set technical direction for the AI/ML team

  • Build agentic orchestration and retrieval flows (RAG, fine-tuning, local vs foundation model decisions, cost optimization)

  • Provide technical leadership and guidance to the 2-3 existing AI/ML engineers

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. Deep computer vision expertise with demonstrated 2D segmentation depth. Foundation model experience (SAM, SAM3, or comparable) and ability to make architectural improvements, not just fine-tune.

  3. Ability to train and improve in-house models from scratch when off-the-shelf models hit their ceiling

  4. Strong research depth (publication track record in CV preferred). Research-track candidates welcome if now hands-on; applied production CV engineers equally welcome.

Nice-to-Have

  • Construction diagrams, floor plans, technical drawings, or architectural CV experience

  • Object detection and classical classifier experience

  • Published research in raster-to-sequence work, floor plan localization, structural priors, or comparable CV subfields

  • Prior technical leadership experience (mentoring or managing AI/ML engineers)

About Aquila Earth

Aquila Earth is building an infinitely scalable energy network that powers a more abundant, limitless, and sustainable future. The team shoots high-powered lasers at drones to charge them mid-flight, beaming energy through light and converting it into electrical power with hyper-efficient links. Every problem the team solves sits at the bleeding edge of physics and technology.

Aquila is a 15-person team based in Sydney (Marrickville office/lab), just finishing its Series A raise, with plans to double headcount soon. The team is engineering-dense (12 engineers across photovoltaic, optical, laser, mechanical, electronics, and firmware disciplines), with ~40% female representation, which is notably strong for deep tech.

About the Role

As a Senior Mechatronics Engineer at Aquila, you will be at the heart of building a mechatronics system that delivers energy through light. You will work end-to-end on novel solutions to problems no one has ever solved before, contributing across the optical beam steering, control systems, and safety system domains.

You will build and own Aquila's mechatronic stack end-to-end: from actuators and sensors, through the electronics that drive them, to the firmware that ties it all together. A rare chance to design, test, and shape foundational architecture from the ground up. Aquila works in rotating project pods, so you will collaborate with electronics, mechanical, firmware, optics, and laser engineers to deliver integrated systems that achieve what no one in the world has done before, on timelines no one would think possible.

What You'll Own

  • Develop optical gimbals that can point an invisible laser within a few mm of a drone flying kilometers away

  • Design, implement, and validate complex MIMO controllers and observers to achieve high-accuracy drone tracking at long distances

  • Design, build, and validate high-accuracy test rigs that precisely simulate laser beam infringement with microsecond-level repeatability

  • Own the mechatronic stack end-to-end: actuators, sensors, electronics, firmware

  • Contribute to greenfield projects with full ownership of higher-performance system redesigns, especially around precision beam steering and safety system timing

  • Collaborate across rotating project pods with electronics, mechanical, firmware, optics, and laser engineers

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. Strong end-to-end mechatronics systems experience built from scratch, including actuator/sensor selection and integration

  2. Real-world high-performance control systems experience, with hands-on work on hard real-time systems where existing solutions and industry precedent do not exist

  3. First-principles problem solving: comfortable building from scratch when no playbook exists, energized by problems you have not solved before

  4. C/C++ familiarity for real-time microcontroller firmware or embedded software development

  5. Bench-level electronics debugging: comfortable diving into schematics, debugging circuits, and evaluating real-world system performance with standard electronic bench equipment

  6. 3+ years of industry experience (exceptional earlier-career candidates considered)

Nice-to-Have

  • Prior startup or scrappy engineering company experience with demonstrated end-to-end ownership

  • Experience with or genuine curiosity around functional safety, especially bridging code and high-power lasers

  • Experience in robotics, aerospace, or similar product-development environments

Compensation

  • Base: $140,000 - $200,000 AUD

  • Equity: ~0.1% range, standard 4-year vest schedule

  • Visa: Visa sponsorship is supported for international candidates relocating to Australia

  • Location: Sydney, Australia (Marrickville). 5 days a week in-office, ~40 hours, with some flexibility (3 in-office + 2 from home for some team members)

You'll spend most of your day talking to customers, leading implementation and onboarding for net-new customers (the team onboards 5-8 net-new customers per week), and shaping the product based on what you see in the field.

responsibilitiesHtml:
About the Strala

We deliver optimal claims outcomes to insurance companies. Not active. Not output. Outcomes. Every product decision, operational improvement, and line of code is held to this standard.

We are rebuilding claims processing, with the ambition to process every claim in the world. That requires long-term thinking, world-class execution, and people committed to doing things the hard but correct way.

About the Role

We sell to large, established companies where claims are seen as a cost center rather than a strategic business driver. Our buyers are senior, our sales cycles are long, and trust is the currency that moves deals. Growth at Strala is not about volume; it is about precision.

We are building a marketing function from the ground up, and we need someone who rigorously tracks performance so we can make confident decisions about what to do next. This role owns measurement and experimentation first, with some channel execution expected. 

This is a role for someone who is rigorously analytical first, and a marketer second. You will build the measurement system that the growth function runs on, and you will be honest about what the data does and does not tell us. 

This is a full-time, in-office role located in San Francisco, CA. We offer relocation assistance.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

  • Build and maintain marketing measurement infrastructure, UTM tracking, CRM source tagging, pipeline attribution, and channel reporting

  • Design experiments across channels with clear hypotheses, controlled setups, and honest readouts regardless of outcome

  • Report on marketing performance with intellectual honesty, what is working, what is not, and what we cannot yet conclude

  • Analyze campaign and events data to surface insights that inform budget allocation and channel prioritization

  • Support channel execution, such as LinkedIn campaign set up, as the operational deployment layer

  • Define and standardize funnel metrics so marketing, sales, and leadership are working from the same definitions

  • Identify gaps in our measurement before we spend more money on channels we cannot yet evaluate

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

  • 0–3 years of experience in an analytical role, the background matters less than the rigor you bring to it

  • You start with the data and let it shape your conclusions, not the other way around

  • Strong grasp of experimentation design, you know what a clean test looks like and why sample size and control conditions matter

  • Comfortable working with marketing analytics tools and CRM platforms

  • Intellectually honest, you are as comfortable reporting a null result as a positive one

  • Clear communicator, you can explain what the data shows and what it does not show to a non-technical audience

  • Comfort with ambiguity, you can make directional recommendations when the data is thin without overstating your confidence

NICE TO HAVE

  • Experience in insurance, finance, or fintech

  • Experience with CRM platforms and marketing automation

  • Experience building measurement infrastructure from scratch rather than inheriting a working system

OUR VALUES

Ambition. We want to win and push for the highest standard.

Performance. We move fast, think in systems, and make decisions for the long term.

Ownership. When we see a problem, we step up and fix it.

Spirit. We operate with clarity, optimism, and meritocracy.

About the Role

You'll be responsible for opening doors, generating conviction, and creating high-quality opportunities for Athena in the US market. Working at the sharp edge of category creation, you'll test messages, earn attention, and learn what resonates before the playbook exists. You'll partner closely with AEs and founders to shape how Athena is positioned to HR, Finance, and Transformation leaders across the US.

What You'll Own

Must-Have

  1. 3+ years of BDR, SDR, or commercial role experience, with demonstrated ability to generate outbound pipeline in B2B SaaS

  2. Proven track record of opening enterprise accounts and closing deals in a hunter-focused motion (100% outbound, no inbound support)

  3. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to craft personalized, thoughtful outreach that resonates

  4. High agency and comfort operating in ambiguity: evolving priorities, partial context, changing messages, and the absence of a defined playbook

  5. In-person in San Francisco; 9am to 5pm Monday through Friday minimum, with flexibility to extend hours as intensity demands

Nice-to-Have

  • Track record of selling to emerging categories or competitive, complex landscapes where you had to build credibility and differentiation

  • Founder or early-stage startup experience, or having built and tested something yourself, even a small project or business

Compensation

tl;dr: We’re automating compliance for banks and fintechs with AI agents that work like human analysts – on a browser. Demand is exploding, and we’re expanding our engineering team to move faster & meet our 6-month roadmap. If you love building end-to-end systems, shipping fast and tackling hard problems, we should talk.

Background

Before you can move money or open an account, someone has to make sure you’re not a criminal. That’s compliance – and it’s broken.

Sphinx builds AI analysts that work inside browsers, APIs, and internal systems just like humans — automating AML, KYC, KYB, and transaction monitoring end-to-end.

Why Join Sphinx

  1. Massive, unsexy market: Banks spend $50B a year hiring thousands of analysts to review alerts and fill out reports by hand. The space has seen very little innovation, and customers complain about our most well-funded competitors weekly. It's not glamorous – until you realize you're building the intelligence layer that protects the entire financial system.

  2. We have never lost a deal to a competitor: Yes you heard that right, we’ve won every RFP we’ve been in.

  3. Small team, big surface area: Our co-founders previously sold an AI company & have built ML systems that scaled to millions of users and closed deals with major banks. The rest of our team in SF includes PhDs, industry experts, and competitive coders.

  4. Hard tech: we’re going from zero to one; our tech is our moat.

  5. Zero startup bullshit: we’re not chasing investors, we’re chasing customers. We’re trusted by leading banks and fintechs across the U.S., Canada, Europe, and LatAm. They’ve seen 90% less manual work, 4× lower costs.

Technical Challenges

1. Browser Agents for the Invisible Web

Most financial crime data isn't accessible via APIs – it lives in legacy systems, government portals, and third-party platforms. We're building agents that navigate these systems like humans do: clicking, scrolling, interpreting unstructured data, and adapting to interface changes. This requires computer vision, DOM understanding, and robust error handling at scale.

2. The Global Risk Graph

Risk doesn’t stop at borders, and neither can we. Our agents operate across languages and regulations, reconciling entities hidden behind shell structures and mismatched disclosures. Each check enriches a single, evolving graph of people, companies, and signals — a global risk intelligence network that never forgets.

3. Decisions at the Speed of Money

Payments don't wait for compliance. We process risk signals at the same speed money moves – millions of transactions, thousands of entities, sub-second decisions. Doing this right on AWS means distributed inference, caching, queue orchestration, and self-healing data pipelines.

4. Deep Research without Hallucinations

Out-of-the-box deep research agents easily confuse entities that look similar. ChatGPT isn’t going to be able to tell us whether John Smith is a terrorist. We’re building our own deep research pipeline to ensure LLMs don’t mix up facts from different people/companies.

What We Look For

  • You solve problems end-to-end: Our team owns features vertically. You'll architect agent behaviors, build backend systems, optimize ML pipelines, and ship product features – often in the same week.

  • You have a high bar for quality: In financial crime, "mostly working" isn't good enough. You obsess over edge cases, build robust error handling, and ship systems that institutions trust with billions in transactions.

  • You want to push AI agent capabilities: We're at the frontier of what's possible with AI agents in production. You'll experiment with the latest models, design novel agentic workflows, and solve problems that don't have Stack Overflow answers.

  • You communicate with clarity: We move fast with minimal process. You need to articulate tradeoffs, communicate blockers, and make technical decisions with limited information.

  • You're energized by impact: Our customers protect the financial system from criminals. Your code directly prevents money laundering and terrorism financing. That matters.

  • You hate meetings: You would much rather focus your time on building, being productive, and shipping code

About the Company

Quill is building an agent system to ensure data reliability. Every company relies on systems of record (CRMs, ERPs) that inevitably fill with messy data, and in the age of AI it's getting worse: AI tools write slop into these systems faster than teams can clean it. That broken data breaks everything downstream. Quill restructures and links company data into a graph that agents can actually operate on, then uses its own agent system to clean data autonomously with governed, human-in-the-loop workflows.

The company raised $4.5M in pre-seed funding and is well-capitalized with several years of runway. The product is live with design partners in daily active usage. Both co-founders are ex-Palantir and led functions at startups (head of engineering and head of growth, respectively); one is a second-time founder.

About the Role

Quill is hiring its first founding engineers. These hires define how the product vision is built: the platform is live with initial users, and the work now is to scale it, incorporate learnings from design partners, and keep pace with every new model release.

The primary responsibility is building the product, but at this stage, that means talking to customers: understanding their problems, building the solution, getting direct feedback, and monitoring usage. The right profile is a full-stack leaning backend with good product intuition. The culture is high-ownership rather than mandated hours: the team hires people who are ambitious and motivated enough that their intensity comes from personal standards, not a schedule. This is also a genuine founder-track seat: joining pre-seed and learning sales, fundraising, and company building from experienced operators.

What You'll Own

  • Build the core Quill platform: the data restructuring layer, company graph, and agent system

Must-Have

  • Product and design sensibility on top of backend depth

About Lane Technologies, Inc.

responsibilitiesHtml:
About e3Group

e3 Group is a San Francisco AI company rebuilding freight brokerage around autonomous agents. We put voice and email negotiation, load matching, document processing, fraud detection, and legacy-system modernization into production for real brokerages — the unglamorous, high-stakes workflows that move freight and money every day. We're small, founder-led, and shipping fast: our agents do real work in front of paying customers, where a wrong number or a dropped call has consequences.

About the Role

We're hiring full-stack engineers who can build production AI end-to-end and own it. This isn't a feature factory — you'll take a problem from the first customer call through the product decision, the code, the deploy, and the traces you watch afterward, then do it again the next week. The surface is real full-stack (React, Next.js, Python), but the center of gravity is applied AI: LLM-driven voice and email agents, streaming speech pipelines, tool-calling with hard guardrails, retrieval, and the evals that keep any of it trustworthy.

It's a high bar, and we'd rather be upfront about how we actually evaluate people — because it's exactly how we run interviews:

  • We go straight at the biggest claim on your resume. Tell us what you personally built, how it works under the hood, how you measured whether it was right, what broke, and what you changed. "My team did that" is fine — as long as you're clear about your part.

  • Evaluation is non-negotiable. If your answer to "how did you know this was correct before any user told you?" is spot-checks or a good prompt, that's a flag. Golden sets, regression and hallucination checks, and tool-call correctness are the language we want.

  • Voice and agents are the domain: streaming, barge-in, latency budgets, and deterministic checks around anything an LLM can get wrong — prices, terms, actions.

  • Think from first principles. Reason about scale, cost, and context limits from scratch; reach for embeddings, retrieval, and reranking before brute force.

  • Work like an AI-native engineer. Claude Code and Codex are daily tools, and you can verify what they produce instead of trusting it blindly.

We're not chasing perfect. Some of our best hires needed a nudge on hard problems — what mattered was getting to the right answer, reasoning honestly, and owning their thinking.

Note: This role is specifically focused on candidates based in India and operating in the India Standard Time (IST) timezone. The requirements and candidate pedigree expectations for this role are held to a higher bar given the India-timezone focus. Only candidates currently residing in India and able to work IST hours will be considered.


What You'll Own

  • Own features end-to-end and ship them weekly: scope the problem with a customer, build across the stack, deploy, and watch the production traces yourself.

  • Build the voice and email negotiation agents — the speech pipeline (STT, TTS, turn-taking), the LLM orchestration, and the deterministic rules that keep prices and terms correct.

  • Build the evaluation layer: golden datasets, offline and online checks, regression and hallucination testing, and tool-call correctness for everything the agents do.

  • Build retrieval and matching on embeddings and reranking, tuned for cost and latency at real scale.

  • Instrument production observability for three audiences at once: engineers debugging, product verifying correctness, and customers who need to trust the outcome.

  • Bring product judgment — tell the difference between a one-off customer request and a real signal worth building around.


Must-Have

  1. 5+ years shipping production software with real end-to-end ownership across a full stack (Python and TypeScript/React).

  2. Hands-on experience taking LLM features to production — architecture, tool-calling, and retrieval, not just prompting.

  3. Fluency with evaluation and testing for AI systems: how you know something works before a user tells you it doesn't.

  4. Strong system-design fundamentals — streaming, concurrency, SQL, and reasoning about scale and cost from first principles.

  5. Comfort with ambiguity and high-stakes calls on limited data, plus generative AI tooling (Claude Code, Codex) as daily instruments you direct and verify.


Nice-to-Have

  • Voice or real-time systems experience: STT/TTS, barge-in, latency budgets, telephony.

  • Founding or early-stage engineer background — evidence you can operate without a playbook.

  • Functional languages (OCaml, Haskell, Scala, Rust) or hardware description languages as a signal of depth and range.

  • Multi-agent orchestration, negotiation flows, or other complex tool-use systems.

  • Open-source work or personal projects shipping at scale; competitive programming as a supplementary signal.

About the Company

Tenex embeds elite teams directly into Fortune 500 operations to find the best that actually move the business and ship the work that makes them AI-native. Anthropic and OpenAI are formal partners, and Tenex sits in the room with their Applied AI teams on real client problems; Vercel, Lovable, and other leading AI companies also partner with Tenex. Tenex was the partner Anthropic named for the Claude for Small Business launch, delivering AI fluency training across 10 US cities, with workflows it built now shipping within Claude for Small Business.

Fully bootstrapped with no outside funding, founded about a year ago by a team that includes a founder with a prior successful company under their belt. Grew from 5 people to 40 in a year, with 80 expected by the end of the quarter and 150-200 by year's end. Beyond consulting, Tenex is exploring joint ventures with clients that combine client distribution with Tenex's technical capability, plus its own IP products going to market independently.

About the Role

Tenex works in pods: a small group of strategists and engineers embeds with a client, learns the domain, and owns the problem end-to-end. Forward Deployed Engineers make the strategists' bets real by working as genuine client-facing software engineers who design, develop, and maintain modern web and agentic applications.

The bar is high agency and high urgency, with less weight on where someone trained and more on what they've actually built. The pace is real, and the standard is that work ships and lands: what counts is whether the workflow is still running on Monday morning when nobody from Tenex is in the room, not the demo. Most people who thrive here describe it as the steepest growth of their careers; the trade-off is not having a year to perfect any single system. This is not a mandated always-on culture, but it is not a standard 40-hour week either: if a deliverable isn't done by Friday, the expectation is to grind through the weekend to land it right, not to wait until Monday.

Tenex also considers intact teams of two to five people (from a pivoting venture, a layoff, or simply a group ready to build together) as a unit, running them through the same bar as individual hires and extending offers to the whole team at once.

What You'll Own

  • Design, build, and maintain modern web and agentic applications directly for Fortune 500 clients

  • Own technical initiatives end-to-end, from architecture through production delivery

  • Operate with high autonomy in ambiguous, fast-moving client environments

  • Present technical work and architecture directly to clients in a clear, consultative way

  • Travel to client sites roughly once a month to work in person with stakeholders

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 3+ years of professional software engineering experience (sweet spot 3-8 years, no hard cap)

  2. Demonstrated experience designing, developing, and maintaining modern web or agentic applications

  3. Experience leading technical initiatives as a tech lead, team lead, founding engineer, or comparable high-ownership capacity

  4. Comfortable operating with high autonomy in ambiguous situations

  5. Genuine client-facing or customer-facing experience: comfortable presenting technical work directly to non-technical stakeholders

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience as a co-founder or CTO at a tech startup

  • Computer science or engineering degree

  • Founded or contributed early at a small AI software development shop, even without major traction

  • Comfortable using agentic coding tools as part of daily workflow

--

Tenex pays a guaranteed base with an uncapped variable that scales directly with shipped work, tracked through an internal story-point system tied to client engagements.

Salary base: $180,000 

Variable structure: a quarterly bonus once an engineer is ramped up. 

Typical outcomes: engineers in good standing generally earn an additional $10,000-$15,000 per quarter beyond base pay; top performers have earned $60,000-$80,000 in a single quarter.

Additional upside: performance-based, discretionary bonus becomes available on top of the story-point bonus as leveling frameworks roll out.

About the Role

The Mid-Market Account Executive is a full-cycle, closing-focused individual contributor converting qualified opportunities into closed-won revenue with mid-market RIA and wealth management firms in the $25,000 to $100,000 ACV range, on sales cycles of roughly 60 to 90 days. Leads come from marketing, the Target Account Development Representative, and the Head of Sales, and the AE owns the deal end to end: discovery, demo coordination with the Solutions Consultant, proposal building, negotiation, and close. This role targets StratiFi's sweet spot: firms that do not yet have a comparable solution and that can be won in 60 to 90 days, with a $1,000,000 ARR annual quota.

What You'll Own

  • Own the full sales cycle from qualified opportunity to signed contract for mid-market advisory firms ($25,000 to $100,000 ACV), targeting $1,000,000 ARR annually

  • Maintain a clean, accurate HubSpot pipeline with disciplined stage progression, current notes, clear next steps, and realistic close dates updated weekly

  • Proactively build and tailor pricing proposals based on firm size, product fit, and competitive positioning

  • Build trust-based relationships with decision-makers through consultative, discovery-led engagement

  • Coordinate with the Solutions Consultant on demos and execute clean, comprehensive handoffs to the Customer Success Manager at close

Must-Have

  1. 3+ years as a full-cycle Account Executive closing mid-market SaaS deals in the $25,000 to $100,000 ACV range with roughly 60 to 90 day sales cycles

  2. 2+ years in wealth management, financial services, or fintech sales, with credible fluency in RIAs, custodians, compliance, and fiduciary concepts from day one

  3. Provable quota attainment of 90%+ for at least one full year, with documentation available to share

  4. Demonstrated pipeline discipline: accurate CRM data maintained without prompting and reliable forecasting (HubSpot or comparable CRM)

  5. Prior experience at a small or growth-stage company (under 100 employees), thriving without a polished playbook

About Eli Health

Eli Health is making continuous hormone monitoring possible through its flagship product, the Hormometer, the first instant hormone monitoring platform to deliver results from saliva to mobile app. Developed over six years of R&D and more than 2,000 product iterations, the platform turns hormones into measurable, trackable signals for stress, endurance, sleep, and more. The team is approximately 25 full-time employees, with a dozen additional contractors and advisors, and is based in Montreal.

About the Role

Eli ships a regulated physical product across borders and is scaling fast. The Supply Chain and Fulfillment Lead will own everything between Eli's suppliers and its customers' doorsteps: sourcing, procurement, inventory, logistics, and order fulfillment, including the complexity of Canada-to-US cross-border shipping and customs. This is an individual contributor role today, with a clear pathway to build and lead the full operations function as the company grows. The right person will report directly to the founder and be positioned to evolve into a Head of Operations over time.

What You'll Own

  • Own the end-to-end supply chain: vendor selection, qualification, audits, long-term relationship management, and backup sourcing for all critical components

  • Eliminate cross-border delays and customs friction in Canada-to-US shipping, managing carrier selection, 3PL relationships, and importer-of-record structures

  • Build and roll out inventory-tracking and procurement-planning systems that give leadership real-time visibility into inventory levels, landed costs, and order status

  • Drive COGS reduction through vendor negotiations, alternative sourcing, and process improvements as order volume scales

  • Own the interface between supply chain and manufacturing on materials planning and production scheduling

  • Set performance standards and accountability for all external partners: suppliers, freight forwarders, 3PLs, and carriers

Must-Have

  1. 3 to 7 years of hands-on supply chain, procurement, and fulfillment experience at a physical product company, with end-to-end ownership rather than a contributor role on a large team

  2. Demonstrated experience managing cross-border shipping between Canada and the US or comparable complexity, including customs, duties, carrier selection, and importer-of-record structures

  3. Experience in a regulated or quasi-regulated consumer product space such as consumer health, food, diagnostics, medical devices, or skincare, where quality and compliance are required even without strict mandates

  4. Proven ability to operate at both strategic and execution levels: capable of negotiating a freight contract and troubleshooting a stuck shipment in the same day

  5. Startup experience or equivalent high-agility environment, with the ability to operate without established playbooks and build systems from scratch

  6. Willingness to work in-person in Montreal at startup hours

Nice-to-Have

  • Engineering or technical background combined with supply chain or manufacturing experience, well-suited for a regulated hardware product

  • Experience scaling fulfillment to hundreds of thousands of orders per month at a Series A to C startup with a team under 50

  • Prior experience with D2C fulfillment in the regulated space (food, skincare, consumer health, diagnostics)

  • Background at companies in the consumer health wearables or adjacent hardware space (for example, early-stage roles at companies like Eight Sleep, Whoop, or Oura)

What We Value

Eli is a small team doing hard things, and these five values guide who thrives here:

  • Grit. We take failure, learn from it, and keep going. Much of what we have built was called impossible when we started.

  • Openness. We have frank conversations, give and take feedback directly, and leave ego at the door.

  • Purpose. We want people who are here because they care about what we are building, not just because it is a good role.

  • Ownership. Nobody here says "it's not my job." We roll up our sleeves and get the work done, whoever we are.

  • Discerning. We go back to first principles, ask the obvious questions others skip, and find the simplest way to do things rather than assuming it can't be done.

Benefits

  • Private Medical and Dental Insurance: Comprehensive coverage through Canada Life for you and your family, including prescription drugs, dental (basic and major), vision, paramedical services (physiotherapy, massage, psychotherapy, and more), short and long-term disability, critical illness insurance, and mental health support ( $1,500/year). Coverage begins on your start date.

  • Employee Assistance Program: Includes industry-leading mental health assistance, a telemedicine app, and 24/7 care through a network of providers. 

  • Group RRSP: Access to a Group RRSP through Empire Life, with pre-tax payroll contributions, professionally managed funds including target-date options, and no vesting period — your contributions are yours immediately.

  • Free Access to Bota Bota Spa: Relax and recharge with unlimited complimentary access to Bota Bota Spa in Montréal.

  • Flexible Working Hours: Adapt your work schedule to better suit your productivity and personal commitments.

  • Free Use of Certain Facilities: Enjoy certain company facilities after hours, subject to availability.

  • Eligibility for Future Employee Benefits: Access to any additional benefits that may be introduced by the company in the future.

  • Office Perks: Complimentary meals, snacks and beverages at the office.

Compensation

  • Base: CAD 80,000 to CAD 150,000

  • Equity: competitive equity

About Decagon

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences.

Our technology enables industry-defining enterprises like Avis Budget Group, Block’s Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas to deploy AI agents that power personalized, deeply satisfying interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel.

We’re building a future where customer experiences are being redefined from support tickets and hold music to faster resolutions, richer conversations, and deeper relationships. We’re proud to be backed by world-class investors who share that vision, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, Index Ventures, and many others.

We’re an in-office company, driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity. Our values, Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner’s Mindset, and The Polymath Principle, shape how we work and grow as a team.

About the Role

Decagon is hiring Customer Engineers and Agent Builders to own the end-to-end execution of AI agent builds for enterprise customers, from initial scoping through launch and iteration. This is a highly technical delivery role: agent builders write and configure key components, validate integrations, and interface directly with senior technical stakeholders on the customer side.

The split between technical build work and customer-facing work is dynamic and shifts with the customer lifecycle, generally landing close to 50/50 or 60/40 technical-to-customer-facing. This is a fast-moving, hands-on culture: not a traditional 9-to-5, but not an always-on grind either. Communication matters enormously in this seat: the team's internal bar is whether they'd feel confident handing this person off to walk the CEO through their work directly.

What You'll Own

  • End-to-end execution of AI agent builds for enterprise customers, from scoping through launch and iteration

  • Write and maintain key agent-building artifacts and configure agent behavior for quality, reliability, and business outcomes

  • Configure and validate guardrails for safe, compliant, predictable agent performance

  • Set up, test, and validate customer integrations (ticketing systems and comparable), building any tools or workflows needed

  • Interface directly with senior technical stakeholders at customers to define success criteria and drive delivery against timelines

  • Partner closely with Agent PMs, Engineering, Design, and GTM teams to deliver consistent, repeatable agent builds

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 3-5 years of experience in a technical customer-facing role (solutions engineering, forward-deployed engineering, technical consulting, implementation engineering, technical PM, or comparable); Toronto requires 5-7 years, given the founding nature of that seat

  2. Strong Python proficiency: this is a hard requirement, unlike most Decagon engineering roles, which are language-agnostic

  3. Comfortable writing code, working with APIs, and building or validating integrations end-to-end

  4. Experience delivering production-grade customer solutions requiring structured execution, testing, and iteration

  5. Clear communicator who can translate requirements into implementation plans and drive delivery with senior technical stakeholders

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience building with or around LLMs and AI agents (prompting, evaluation, guardrails, tooling, workflow design)

  • Experience with enterprise SaaS integrations (ticketing systems, CRM, data pipelines) and associated security or compliance considerations

  • Computer Science, Engineering, or Math degree, or equivalent technical experience

  • Strong product instinct: can write crisp requirements documents and define success metrics

About the Company

Contour is building the AI operating layer for forward-deployed engineering (FDE) and professional services teams. Implementation work has never been more needed, driven by surging demand for forward-deployed engineering across businesses of every size and industry. Contour helps teams run deliveries more smoothly and efficiently, reinventing a $400B+ market.

Seed-stage, based in San Francisco, raised $11.2M, co-led by Lightspeed Ventures and Chemistry. Team of 5 full-time plus 3 interns: two founding engineers and one founding operations person, alongside the two co-founders. One co-founder previously built a voice agent startup (YC W24), was an early product and business hire at Cartesia (helping grow it from zero to multiple millions in ARR), and spent time investing at Chemistry, where they saw the FDE scaling challenge firsthand across portfolio companies. The other co-founder was the first founding engineer and later head of engineering at Conversion (an AI enterprise marketing company), leading a 15-person engineering team and building roughly half of that company's product.

About the Role

Contour is hiring Full-Stack Engineers to own and lead engineering projects across the company's product offerings, working closely with customer-facing teams to build systems that solve critical implementation problems. The role is full-stack leaning, with meaningful frontend work: one of the platforms being built is customer-facing, so product taste matters alongside engineering depth.

The company is heavily bottlenecked on full-stack build capacity right now. Engineers will make some decisions that directly affect the customer product, but this is not a customer-facing seat: no calls with customers, no hiring responsibilities. The codebase spans phases: some polished and built for scale, some genuinely greenfield, so comfort building from scratch is important. Reports to the founders.

What You'll Own

  • Craft interfaces trusted by enterprise teams on their most critical workflows

  • Engineer agentic workflows that stay performant under real-world load

  • Architect the full stack behind high-performance applications

  • Retrieve information over large corpora of unstructured enterprise data

  • Evaluate LLMs across the application layer to determine what actually works in production

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 3+ years of strong programming experience (2-3+ years considered based on caliber)

  2. Proficiency in Python and TypeScript

  3. Strong customer intuition, even without direct customer-facing responsibilities

  4. History of persistence and getting hard things done; thrives in a fast-paced environment

Nice-to-Have

  • Prior startup experience with high ownership, ideally having taken projects from zero to meaningful scale

  • Genuine side projects or personal builds that demonstrate love of the craft, not just professional output

  • Comfort building greenfield products from scratch, not just maintaining existing systems

  • Strong product taste, given the customer-facing surfaces being built

Ollive AI Inc is hiring its first Founding AI/ML Engineer to own the evaluation engine at the core of the platform, the system that continuously tests, scores, and quantifies risk in customer AI agents. This is the primary technical undertaking for at least the next six to twelve months, encompassing both the evals pipeline and the synthetic testing infrastructure that powers simulation at scale. The engineer will work hands-on alongside the CTO and founding team, experimenting with open-weight models, architecting RL loops for auto-improvement, and taking the existing system to production-grade depth. What You'll Own

  • Own and advance the evals engine: design, build, and iterate the evaluation pipeline that measures and quantifies risk in customer AI agents

  • Architect and establish RL loops, including agentic RL loops, to give the platform an auto-improvement capability

  • Build and maintain synthetic testing infrastructure: generate and simulate adversarial scenarios at scale to stress-test AI agent behavior

  • Experiment with frontier and open-source models from HuggingFace deployed via PipeShift, benchmarking model performance and maintaining production throughput

  5. Proficiency in Python and the HuggingFace ecosystem (Transformers and related tooling) for model experimentation and deployment

Human Delta is the AI adoption engine for American enterprises, building the operating layer that makes enterprise AI reliable, safe, and genuinely usable at scale. Must-Have

  1. 2 to 5 years of experience in a technical, customer-facing role

  • Experience with LLMs, retrieval systems, knowledge bases, or search

About the Company

Sunset was founded to help founders. It started by supporting startups through shutting down, and has since expanded into unlocking a new revenue stream for all types of businesses. The insight underneath it: the data every company generates day to day (collaboration, communication, building) is some of the most valuable training data in the world. Public and synthetic data can only take frontier models so far, and the next generation of model progress depends on real, proprietary data grounded in how actual businesses operate. Sunset is a primary source of it, partnering directly with the frontier AI labs building what comes next.

The company has scaled from $0 to a multi-million run rate in a matter of months, doing multiple million in revenue in a single recent month. It is backed by top-tier investors including Floodgate, Afore, Ludlow, and Hustle Fund, and recently raised again. This is a rare ground-floor seat at a category-defining business.

About the Role

As a Business Development Representative (Data Partnerships), you will be the first point of contact for operating companies exploring a new revenue stream through data licensing. Your primary responsibility is building a qualified pipeline for the Data Partnerships Account Executives while holding a high standard in every interaction. This is a high-volume, high-quality motion: you will drive outbound at pace without ever letting the quality of a conversation slip.

This is the harder of the two SDR seats, and deliberately so. You are reaching out to healthy, ongoing companies with no urgent trigger pushing them toward yes, so persistence matters even more here than in a typical SDR role. You will partner closely with the Account Executives on sourcing, strategy, and deal handoff, and report directly to the Founder. Reps who can stay relentless through hundreds of no's while remaining sharp, credible, and technically conversant about the data and de-identification angle will do well.

What You'll Own

  • Consistently hit or exceed monthly targets for qualified calls booked

  • Generate a high volume of opportunities through personalized outreach to operating companies

  • Partner closely with Account Executives on sourcing, strategy, and deal handoff

  • Continuously find ways to improve and iterate on outreach and process

  • Speak credibly to the data licensing and de-identification angle when it comes up

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 12+ months of BDR experience, or a consulting, closing, or operations role with clear quota ownership.

  2. Relentlessness with no urgent trigger to lean on: comfortable going after healthy, ongoing companies and persisting through hundreds of no's.

  3. Technically sharp enough to speak to the data and de-identification angle if it comes up.

  4. High EQ and IQ: sharp and credible, not a stereotypical hard-sell rep.

  5. Excited to build in person, 5 days a week, from the Dumbo office, working hard toward world-class performance.

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience in consulting or operations

  • Internship or early-career experience in a performance-based or client-facing environment

  • A track record of iterating on outreach and improving conversion

  • Comfort operating in an early-stage environment without a fixed playbook

About the Role

Candor is bringing its data-loss-prevention engine down to the endpoint. The AI detection engine that decides whether a data movement is suspicious is already being built in-house by the founding team. What is needed now is an engineer who has built and shipped production Windows endpoint agents and can lead that work end-to-end. You will define the agent's internal structure, reverse-engineer the relevant Windows system APIs, and emit the telemetry the platform needs: data uploads to the browser, how data moves on the endpoint, web searches, file renaming, and other indicators of suspicious activity streamed back to the backend for processing.

This is a teach-and-build role. The founding team will define the telemetry targets and what the agent should emit; you will own how it is done. You will have substantial latitude over architecture and will actively guide a highly technical founder who is looking to learn from you. Getting this right is non-trivial: a mistake at this layer can trigger blue screens of death across an entire customer fleet, so hands-on experience is essential.

  • Design, build, and ship the Windows endpoint agent end-to-end, from system-level telemetry capture to backend streaming

  • Reverse-engineer and integrate the Windows system APIs required to observe data movement safely without destabilizing the OS

  • Emit the defined telemetry set (browser data uploads, endpoint data movement, web searches, file renaming, and other suspicious-activity indicators)

  • Set and evolve the agent architecture, and level up a technical founding team through direct collaboration

Must-Have

  5. High autonomy and strong communication: able to lead architecture decisions independently and teach a technical founder, rather than relying on separate deployment or platform teams.

Nice-to-Have

  • Prior experience at a DLP or insider-risk company (for example, Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Cyberhaven, or Microsoft Defender)

  • Browser extension or cross-platform telemetry experience

The company raised its seed round two years ago and is trusted by security leaders at global enterprises, including a public endorsement from Chevron's CISO. responsibilitiesHtml:
About the Company

Candor Security is a YC-backed company building agentic data loss prevention and insider risk detection for modern enterprises. Rather than drowning security teams in static rules and false positives, Candor ties every action to the person, pattern, and intent behind it, then surfaces only the handful of incidents that genuinely warrant attention, with the full context already assembled. The platform is built by AI experts from AMD, JPMorgan, NASA, and Uber, is SOC 2 Type II, and is based in San Francisco.

The company raised its seed round two years ago and is trusted by security leaders at global enterprises, including a public endorsement from Chevron's CISO. Candor recently moved from an agentless architecture to a native endpoint approach across macOS, Windows, and Linux, plus a browser extension, and its sales pipeline filled almost immediately after that decision. This is a high-demand, high-momentum moment to help build the endpoint layer from the ground up.

About the Role

Candor is bringing its data-loss-prevention engine down to the endpoint. The AI detection engine that decides whether a data movement is suspicious is already being built in-house by the founding team. What is needed now is an engineer who has built and shipped production macOS endpoint agents and can lead that work end-to-end. You will define the agent's internal structure, reverse-engineer the relevant macOS system APIs, and emit the telemetry the platform needs: data uploads to the browser, how data moves on the endpoint, web searches, file renaming, and other indicators of suspicious activity streamed back to the backend for processing.

This is a teach-and-build role. The founding team will define the telemetry targets and what the agent should emit; you will own how it is done. You will have substantial latitude over architecture and will actively guide a highly technical founder who is looking to learn from you. Getting this right is non-trivial: a mistake at this layer can destabilize every machine in a customer's fleet, so hands-on experience is essential.

What You'll Own

  • Design, build, and ship the macOS endpoint agent end-to-end, from system-level telemetry capture to backend streaming

  • Reverse-engineer and integrate the macOS system and endpoint security APIs required to observe data movement safely and reliably

  • Emit the defined telemetry set (browser data uploads, endpoint data movement, web searches, file renaming, and other suspicious-activity indicators)

  • Own customer deployment: MDM policy design, staged rollout, and safe agent update mechanisms that do not break customer machines

  • Set and evolve the agent architecture, and level up a technical founding team through direct collaboration

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. Proven experience building and shipping production macOS endpoint agents end-to-end, not just contributing to one component of a large system.

  2. Deep familiarity with macOS system internals: endpoint security and system extension frameworks, kernel-level telemetry, and the constraints of collecting data safely on the endpoint.

  3. Proficiency in Rust, or the ability and willingness to build in Rust; strong C++ is acceptable if paired with a clear technical rationale for the language choice.

  4. Hands-on experience deploying and rolling out endpoint agents at customer scale, including MDM policy design, staged rollout, and update delivery.

  5. High autonomy and strong communication: able to lead architecture decisions independently and teach a technical founder, rather than relying on separate deployment or platform teams.

Nice-to-Have

  • Prior experience at a DLP or insider-risk company (for example, Palo Alto Networks, CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Cyberhaven, or Microsoft Defender)

  • Experience building agents across both macOS and Windows

  • Prior experience at an early-stage startup, not only in large companies

  • Browser extension or cross-platform telemetry experience

Comps 

  • India: $10k–$15k/month

  • LATAM: $11k–$16k/month

  • US: $14k–$19k/month

About the Company

Decagon is the leading conversational AI platform, empowering every brand to deliver concierge customer experiences. Its technology enables industry-defining enterprises to deploy AI agents that power personalized interactions across voice, chat, email, SMS, and every other channel, replacing support tickets and hold music with faster resolutions and richer conversations. Public customers include Avis Budget Group, Cash App and Square, Chime, Oura Health, and Hunter Douglas.

Decagon is backed by world-class investors, including a16z, Accel, Bain Capital Ventures, Coatue, and Index Ventures. It is an in-office company driven by a shared commitment to excellence and velocity, with values (Just Get It Done, Invent What Customers Want, Winner's Mindset, and The Polymath Principle) that shape how the team works and grows.

About the Role

The Customer Engineer, Agent Builder is a post-sales, deployed engineer who owns end-to-end execution of AI agent builds for strategic enterprise customers. This is a highly technical delivery role: you own the implementation work required to launch and scale enterprise-quality agents, partnering with customers and internal teams to define success, translate requirements into build plans, and deliver agents that meaningfully impact the customer's business. The work is dynamic, aiming to stay close to a 50/50 (or 60/40) split between customer-facing engagement and hands-on technical build work, depending on where each customer is in its lifecycle.

This is a newly formed Agent Builder org (stood up earlier this year, currently 7 to 8 people in seat), a specialized technical delivery team responsible for writing and configuring key agent components, validating integrations, and ensuring agents perform reliably at scale. You will work closely with Agent PMs, Agent Success, Engineering, and Go-To-Market teams in tight feedback loops, executing builds, surfacing gaps, and influencing the evolution of Decagon's agent-building platform. Travel is rare. The role is ideal for a software or forward-deployed engineer who wants to pivot into customer-facing delivery and thrives in fast-moving, ambiguous environments.

What You'll Own

  • Own end-to-end architecture and execution of AI agent builds for enterprise customers, from systems design and scoping through implementation, evaluation, and production deployment

  • Design and engineer the core agentic logic governing agent behavior, plus layered guardrails and supervisory controls for safe, compliant, predictable performance across non-deterministic outputs

  • Architect, build, and test integrations with customer systems (data pipelines, CRMs, ticketing systems), including the tools, APIs, and workflows needed for reliable deployment at scale

  • Interface with senior technical stakeholders at customers to define success criteria and system requirements, and drive technical delivery against timelines

  • Diagnose, debug, and resolve probabilistic and technical failures through root-cause analysis, and design evaluation and regression-testing frameworks that guard against performance drift

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 3 to 5 years in a technical, customer-facing role (solutions engineering, forward-deployed engineering, technical consulting, implementation engineering, or technical product), with exceptional candidates at 1+ year considered; Toronto requires 5 to 7 years

  2. Strong Python proficiency: comfortable writing, running, and debugging code and building and validating integrations end-to-end (assessed live, with no AI coding assistants permitted)

  3. Genuine post-sales interest, wanting to go deep on hands-on technical delivery and customer engagement, not pivot toward pre-sales

  4. Exceptional communication skills and executive-ready presence, credible with senior technical stakeholders

  5. Comfort in fast-moving, ambiguous environments, shaping solutions as much as implementing them, and available in the office 5 days per week

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience building with or around LLMs and AI agents (prompting, evaluation, guardrails, tooling, workflow design)

  • Experience with enterprise SaaS integrations (ticketing systems, CRM, data pipelines) and associated security and compliance considerations

  • A Computer Science, Engineering, or Math degree, or equivalent technical background (CS strongly preferred; adjacent quantitative degrees such as Data Science or Data Engineering acceptable)

  • Strong product instinct: crisp PRDs, clear success metrics, and customer insight fed back into the product roadmap
