About the Company

Mason AI is on the frontier of agentic AI for the built world, building the technical leader in AI that checks whether construction blueprints are buildable and safe. Its multimodal agents review blueprints for building-code compliance, becoming domain-experts on things like the ADA and Wildland-Urban Interface rules, with work that directly affects California's built environment within a new hire's first month.

The company grew out of SFYIMBY, the pro-housing organization in San Francisco, and its mission is to solve the housing crisis: if Mason wins, the cost of building housing drops meaningfully and rents get more affordable. It is one of the very few places in tech where an engineer can work directly on housing, and that mission, shared even by its investors, is the company's single strongest draw. Mason has raised $4.3M, is the technical leader in its space with the most progress of any competitor, and its product demo reliably gets strong engineers excited.

About the Role

This is a deeply self-directed founding engineering role at a tiny company (three people, moving to two as the CTO transitions out). The bulk of the work is running experiments end to end on the company's eval framework: generating the hypotheses, implementing the experiments, and analyzing the results to improve the accuracy of multimodal agents that check blueprints for code compliance. The role demands someone independent and self-unblocking who can direct their own work with strong research taste.

Two profiles have worked here: an exceptional software engineer who wants to break into AI research, and an AI/ML engineer already established in the space. The work is heads-down and technical, with only about two hours a week talking to users (occasionally on-site, but this is not a forward-deployed role). Expectations are high: roughly 55 hours a week with weekend availability, in person in SF every day, in exchange for a large chunk of ownership. The company is explicitly betting its future on this hire and the next.

What You'll Own

  • The majority of your time improving the accuracy of Mason's multimodal blueprint-compliance agents, from building autoresearch to improving evals to running sweeps on experimental features you design

  • The full experiment loop: coming up with ideas, implementing them, and rigorously analyzing results on the eval framework

  • Becoming a domain expert on the parts of the building code that matter (ADA, Wildland-Urban Interfaces, structural and fire safety)

  • Wearing hats as needed: computer-vision experiments, lightweight data engineering, internal tooling, and webapp improvements

  • Weekly user contact and product dogfooding, roughly two hours a week

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. Independent and self-unblocking, able to direct your own work with minimal oversight

  2. High velocity, fast at prototyping and shipping experiments

  3. Rigorous about evaluation, with genuine research taste to steer high-risk, high-reward work

  4. Either a strong SWE eager to grow into ML/AI, or an ML/AI engineer already fast at prototyping

  5. Genuine mission alignment with solving the housing crisis

  6. Able to work in person in San Francisco, ~55 hours/week with weekend availability

Nice-to-Have

  • Background at a self-driving car company (e.g. Waymo, Zoox), where evaluation rigor is life-or-death and directly analogous to Mason's work

  • Experience at highly regulated application-layer AI startups (medical, legal) where the cost of mistakes drives serious evaluation discipline

  • Experience at climate-tech startups, which tends to correlate with mission orientation

  • Strong academic background

  • The curiosity of a policy wonk to digest building codes and architectural diagrams

About the Company

Bluejay is building the simulation, observability, and self-improvement layer for Voice AI agents, with a mission to be the trust layer between AI and humanity. Founders Faraz and Rohan left Microsoft and AWS, where they built critical infrastructure for MSFT Copilot and AWS Bedrock. Voice is the hardest modality for AI, and Bluejay builds the evaluation infrastructure to make voice agents reliable enough to succeed with real customers.

In just one year, Google, DoorDash, public healthcare companies, public banks, most drive-through fast-food chains, and corporations across five continents have used Bluejay to understand and improve their Voice AI agents. The company raised a $4M seed in 2025 backed by Floodgate, PeakXV, and YC, and runs comfortably on seven-figure revenue. It handles millions of calls a month, creating hard real-time product and engineering problems. The team is 10 people, punching well above their weight, based in a beautiful office (The Sky) in Union Square. Bluejay believes every company with a publicly facing phone number will use a voice agent within four years.

About the Role

As a Member of Technical Staff, you'll architect and develop systems that simulate, analyze, and evaluate conversational AI agents across voice and multimodal systems, and design resilient, scalable infrastructure on AWS (Lambda, EC2, WebSockets, SIP) to handle millions of real-time conversations. You'll build algorithms and pipelines that surface insights, detect failure modes, and keep agents safe, reliable, and aligned with human intent.

This is a high-bar, full-ownership role on a 10-person team, with proficiency expected across the stack, especially databases, AWS, and AI engineering. It's also customer-facing: you'll work on-site with customers, building, selling, and deploying the product to some of the largest companies in the world. Bluejay wants engineers who obsess over details, can lead a project's technical execution, and have built high-traffic features at scale.

What You'll Own

  • Architecting and developing simulation, analysis, and evaluation systems for conversational AI (voice and multimodal)

  • Resilient, scalable AWS infrastructure (Lambda, EC2, Websockets, SIP) for millions of real-time conversations

  • Algorithms and pipelines that surface insights, detect failure modes, and keep agents safe and aligned

  • Full ownership of your work, across the stack

  • Working on-site with customers to build, sell, and deploy the product

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 1+ years of experience (JD body references 2+; confirm)

  2. High technical bar with proficiency across the stack, specifically databases, AWS, and AI engineering

  3. Ability to obsess over details and lead technical execution, ideally with experience building high-traffic features at scale

  4. An exceptional signal: a strong bachelor's degree and/or prior experience at a top fast-growing startup

  5. Strong communicator and personable (customer-facing role)

  6. Able to work in person in SF, 5 days a week, 9-7

Core Stack

  • Backend: Python, FastAPI, Supabase, Redis, heavy AWS, Websockets, CI/CD

  • AI: Python, Machine Learning, LLMs

  • Voice AI: LiveKit, Deepgram, Cartesia, ElevenLabs, Gemini, and similar

  • DevX: optimized developer setup (skills, MCP integrations, worktrees, heavy task parallelization)

  • Observability: Sentry, PostHog, Grafana, Datadog

Desirable Quirks / Signals

  • Super opinionated about design decisions, with deep intuition from prior systems design

  • A highly optimized developer workflow ("What's your workflow for 100x engineering?")

  • Has handled immense scale as an IC or senior SWE

  • Has been a technical lead who owned projects end to end

The team is five people today, and this hire joins the technical side alongside the CTO and lead software engineer as one of the first ten employees. The role requires someone who is deeply hands-on, capable of reasoning through a six-month hardware roadmap with full architectural clarity, and comfortable making consequential decisions with limited precedent. What You'll Own Own the full PCB design lifecycle: architecture, component selection, layout, and iterative builds from the current prototype toward a fleet-ready cockpit device Make which parts to use and where to get them across the supply chain Plan and execute environmental testing to validate the Wave against heat, vibration, and RF noise conditions in live aircraft Develop and own embedded firmware and edge processing logic as the hardware matures Report directly to the CTO and collaborate with the software engineering team to ensure hardware captures the data the AI analytics layer requires Must-Have 5+ years of hands-on hardware engineering experience, with a demonstrated track record of building and shipping a physical product from scratch, not just hardware operating in demanding conditions (thermal, vibrational, or similar) Startup or similarly lean background where you owned hardware decisions end to end, not a large company where 100 engineers share a single problem domain Ability to fluently walk through a multi-month hardware project plan, reason through architectural trade-offs in real time, and clearly justify design decisions Willingness to work startup hours (9am to 9pm, six days a week) and be in-person in San Francisco five days a week Nice-to-Have Firmware knowledge and experience with embedded systems or real-time operating systems Background building sensor devices or connected hardware in a startup environment Experience with wireless communication modules (cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth) and edge-to-cloud data streaming Exposure to aviation, defense, or other safety-critical regulated hardware environments

About Navi

Navi captures everything a pilot sees and hears during a flight and turns it into automated debrief intelligence, giving flight instructors and squadron commanders sortie-level awareness that has never existed before. The platform is already live at Embry-Riddle, Purdue, UND, Sling Pilot Academy, and the United States Air Force. The company's hardware device, the Wave, sits in the cockpit and streams audio and telemetry data to the cloud in real time, where Navi's AI analytics generate the debrief.

About the Role

This is a founding hardware role at Navi, and the person who fills it owns the physical product end to end: PCB architecture and layout, component sourcing and procurement, environmental testing, embedded firmware, and the build-vs-buy decisions that determine how the Wave scales from its current 3D-printed prototype to a fleet-deployed cockpit device. The team is five people today, and this hire joins the technical side alongside the CTO and lead software engineer as one of the first ten employees. The role requires someone who is deeply hands-on, capable of reasoning through a six-month hardware roadmap with full architectural clarity, and comfortable making consequential decisions with limited precedent.

What You'll Own

  • Own the full PCB design lifecycle: architecture, component selection, layout, and iterative builds from the current prototype toward a fleet-ready cockpit device

  • Make build-vs-outsource decisions on hardware manufacturing, balancing cost, compute requirements, and thermal constraints for an in-cockpit environment

  • Lead component sourcing and procurement, identifying which parts to use and where to get them across the supply chain

  • Plan and execute environmental testing to validate the Wave against heat, vibration, and RF noise conditions in live aircraft

  • Develop and own embedded firmware and edge processing logic as the hardware matures

  • Report directly to the CTO and collaborate with the software engineering team to ensure hardware captures the data the AI analytics layer requires

Must-Have

  1. 5+ years of hands-on hardware engineering experience, with a demonstrated track record of building and shipping a physical product from scratch, not just contributing to one component of a large team effort

  2. Proven ability to design and lay out a PCB independently, including schematic design, component selection, and board bring-up

  3. Experience with component sourcing and procurement: understanding which parts to spec, where to get them, and how those decisions compound over time

  4. Familiarity with environmental and regulatory testing standards for hardware operating in demanding conditions (thermal, vibrational, or similar)

  5. Startup or similarly lean background where you owned hardware decisions end to end, not a large company where 100 engineers share a single problem domain

  6. Ability to fluently walk through a multi-month hardware project plan, reason through architectural trade-offs in real time, and clearly justify design decisions

  7. Willingness to work startup hours (9am to 9pm, six days a week) and be in-person in San Francisco five days a week

Nice-to-Have

  • Firmware knowledge and experience with embedded systems or real-time operating systems

  • Background building sensor devices or connected hardware in a startup environment

  • Experience with wireless communication modules (cellular, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth) and edge-to-cloud data streaming

  • Exposure to aviation, defense, or other safety-critical regulated hardware environments

responsibilities: About the Company LegalCare is building the first primary care-style law firm. It is a team of attorneys spanning 16 practice areas, including family law, employment law, personal injury, and immigration, whose only job is to meet one-on-one with people seeking a lawyer, diagnose exactly what they need, and triage them to the right outside firm or nonprofit. Advice sessions are free to consumers. The firm earns revenue by sharing in the fees partner firms generate from referred clients, between 15 and 35 percent depending on practice area, a structure only available because LegalCare is itself a law firm under the attorney ethical rules. Distribution is the most novel part of the model. LegalCare runs no paid advertising. Instead, it gives other law firms a free AI intake receptionist, a conversational voice agent that connects to their phone system alongside an embeddable web form. Between 10 and 20 percent of the calls consumer-facing firms receive fall outside the services they offer, and when a caller's needs do not match the services offered and the caller consents, the caller is transferred to LegalCare in real time. The company is bootstrapped and founded by a former startup and venture capital attorney. Sixteen practitioners have already signed on across practice areas, the first version of the intake receptionist is built and working, and early outreach to partner firms is converting at a 15 to 20 percent reply rate. The immediate mandate is to take the existing voice AI intake receptionist from a working founder-built prototype to a production-grade system. These are sensitive, high-stakes conversations with people in legal distress, so reliability, privacy, and security are the central engineering problems, not afterthoughts. Alongside the receptionist, the role owns the platform that facilitates referrals between LegalCare and partner firms, including the handling of sensitive client funds. About the Company

Ember is building AI-native infrastructure for the back office of healthcare. Providers do the work and then wait, or never get paid at all, because of administrative burden, payer friction, and denied claims. Ember's platform automates the revenue cycle so provider groups capture the revenue they have already earned, with real-time visibility into financial and operational performance. Customers see net revenue increase by roughly 5 to 15 percent depending on where they start.

Backed by Y Combinator (F24) with $5M raised, Ember is a 20-person Series A company and already profitable. Founder-led sales have produced roughly $6M in closed revenue, with ACVs ranging from $200K to $1.5M and a consistent cadence of five closes per month sustained over the last five months. The buyer is the CFO, the motion is top-down, and legacy revenue cycle incumbents are actively being displaced by AI-native platforms.

About the Role

The sales motion works. The CEO built it, sold it, and is now looking for Account Executives who can scale it with discipline rather than reinvent it. This is one of the first AE seats behind a founder-led motion with proven product-market fit, a short cycle, and a commission plan built for people who want to sell.

The Account Executive owns deals end to end with PE-backed, multi-site specialty provider groups, running a consultative process with C-suite and revenue cycle leadership. Deals in the $200K to $300K range typically close in about a month; $1.5M deals run closer to three months. This is not an order-taking seat: alongside inbound and BDR-generated pipeline, the AE is expected to self-source, diagnose revenue cycle pain, quantify the impact, and align operators on a plan to reduce A/R days and denials. The role reports directly to the CEO and partners with the founders on messaging, pricing, packaging, and objection handling.

What You'll Own

  • A pipeline of PE-backed, multi-site specialty provider groups from first meeting through close, with meaningful self-sourced contribution

  • Structured discovery with CFOs and VPs of Revenue Cycle, plus multi-threading across finance, revenue cycle, IT/EMR, and operations

  • ROI narratives tied to denials, A/R aging, cash acceleration, and staffing load, delivered through crisp demos and executive readouts

  • Evaluation and contracting steps: data access, sample pulls, security review, and workflow fit

  • Conference and trade show pipeline: pre-booked meetings, live lead work, and closed follow-up loops

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 2+ years carrying an individual AE quota in B2B SaaS or healthcare technology, with an attainment history you can walk through deal by deal

  2. Sales experience touching the healthcare revenue cycle: RCM, denials, claims, billing workflows, patient financing, or EHR and practice management platforms

  3. Comfort selling directly to CFO, COO, and revenue cycle leadership, and running a multi-step process across 3 to 6+ stakeholders with real change management

  4. Demonstrated self-sourced pipeline generation, structured discovery and qualification (MEDDICC), and strong CRM and forecasting rigor

  5. Willingness to travel roughly two weeks per month for conferences, onsite meetings, and executive visits, regardless of home base

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience selling into PE-backed healthcare or multi-site provider groups

  • Familiarity with EMRs, clearinghouses, and practice management systems

  • Conference-driven pipeline motion

  • Quantitative academic background

Salary: $150K base + $150K commission at quota ($300K OTE), uncapped with accelerators.

About the Company

Opal Electronics is a consumer hardware company in San Francisco building AI-native devices. The company raised a $40M Series B led by OpenAI, with Samsung, Founders Fund, and the founders of Instagram, Airbnb, and YouTube also on the cap table. Opal operates independently with full creative control over its roadmap.

The team is 22 people working from an SF office with an in-house prototyping lab. Opal previously shipped the C1 and Tadpole cameras and now runs as an R&D studio for consumer products, where each device is its own program rather than an iteration on a single line. Some products are built for mass production, others for smaller and more experimental markets. The first device in the new lineup launches this year. Software is a team of four; hardware is five to six.

About the Role

The companion app is the primary interface to Opal's hardware, which makes this role central rather than peripheral. The work covers BLE and Wi-Fi pairing flows, reconnection and background connectivity, firmware update delivery through the app, and a real-time UI that reflects live device state and streaming data with responsive feedback as conditions change. It also covers surfacing AI capabilities in the app and coordinating between on-device inference and cloud processing.

This role reports to the Software Engineering Manager, who holds a Stanford PhD and previously led R&D at a growth-stage AI voice startup after time at NVIDIA and Google. Because the app sits directly on top of physical hardware, the role is cross-functional by default, working with hardware, firmware, and backend and ML teams throughout. Engineers here own features end-to-end, from architecture through App Store release, and are expected to self-manage in a small team without heavy process.

What You'll Own

  • Device pairing and connectivity: BLE and Wi-Fi pairing flows, reconnection handling, background connectivity, and firmware update delivery through the app

  • Real-time device experience: low-latency UI reflecting live device state and data streams

  • On-device and cloud AI features, coordinating between local inference and cloud processing

  • Companion app architecture: device state, sync, and graceful handling of offline and degraded connectivity

  • Native platform depth: background modes, push notifications, Bluetooth permissions, and battery and performance optimization for an app that is frequently active and connected

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. Strong Swift and SwiftUI/UIKit experience shipping production iOS apps

  2. Experience with Core Bluetooth and/or real-time data streaming

  3. Comfort owning a feature end-to-end: architecture, implementation, testing, and App Store release

  4. Demonstrated ability to work cross-functionally with hardware, firmware, and backend/ML teams

  5. Proven ability to self-manage and operate inside a small engineering team

Nice-to-Have

  • Hardware-paired app experience

  • Experience with connected/IoT devices or wearables, which is highly valued given the nature of the product

  • Startup or small-team experience, particularly at growth-stage companies

  • Personal projects or side builds outside of work

responsibilitiesHtml:
About Luzid

Luzid creates AI agent infrastructure to help companies implement their ERP software solutions. The company has more than 20 employees across offices in San Francisco and Sao Paulo, has reached more than $3M ARR in 11 months, and has raised $21M in funding. The team comes from Stanford, Meta, Two Sigma, Microsoft, and NASA.

About the Role

Luzid is hiring a Deployment Strategist in Sao Paulo to own adoption outcomes for its largest enterprise accounts. SAP transformations fail on adoption, not software, and this role exists to move organizations through the change required to get value from the platform. You will own the deployment plan, drive change management across multi-country stakeholder environments, and report directly to the Deployment Lead. There is no inherited playbook: you will be building the deployment motion while running it, inside some of the largest SAP integrator accounts in the world.

What You'll Own

  • Own the end-to-end deployment plan for enterprise S/4HANA programs, including scope, milestones, quality gates, and go-live readiness

  • Lead change management from stakeholder mapping through enablement and adoption tracking across multi-country, multi-stakeholder environments

  • Translate between technical SAP teams and C-suite sponsors at global integrators and the enterprises they serve

  • Build the deployment playbook from scratch, including templates, quality gates, and onboarding motions, so each subsequent deployment is faster and cleaner

  • Feed product signal back to the founding team based on direct observation of how the platform behaves inside live programs

  • Travel within Brazil to key client sites as needed to protect against churn and ensure in-person engagement at critical milestones

Must-Have

  1. 10 or more years of combined project management and program management experience on enterprise SAP implementations, including direct experience in S/4HANA programs across blueprint, build, test, go-live, and hypercare phases

  2. Demonstrated strength in change management: getting users and organizations to adopt new products or processes in multi-country, multi-stakeholder environments

  3. Track record of owning delivery outcomes and accountability for plans and quality gates across multiple enterprise programs, not just reporting on them

  4. Client-facing delivery experience including presenting to and managing senior and C-suite audiences at large consulting firms or enterprises

  5. Native Portuguese fluency and professional English proficiency

  6. High agency and comfort operating in an early-stage, ambiguous environment without a defined playbook

  7. Willingness to work in person at the Sao Paulo office four days per week (Location: Avenida Nacoes Unidas, 12901 Andares 12, 23, 24, e 25, Brooklin, Sao Paulo, SP, 04578-910)

Nice-to-Have

  • Big 4 or systems-integrator background (Deloitte, KPMG, EY, Accenture, or equivalent)

  • Experience implementing early-stage or emerging software products within large enterprise programs

  • Formal delivery rigor certifications such as SAP Activate, Scrum/PSM, or PMO frameworks

  • Exposure to SAP functional modules including FI, MM, SD, HR, or GRC

  • Founder or entrepreneurial experience alongside a consulting or delivery career

  • Genuine engagement with AI tooling and agentic workflows, including side projects or active use

About JAMPACK AI

Jampack AI is the agentic platform automating wholesale operations for CPG brands. When a brand sells to Walmart, Costco, or any major retailer, the process involves toggling between ten or more disconnected tools, including EDI platforms, freight brokers, invoicing software, and distributor portals. Jampack replaces all of that with intelligent end-to-end automation. Brands like Fishwife, Path Water, Immi, and Ghia save 20+ hours per week, reduce freight costs by 15%, and achieve 50x faster order-to-invoice cycles. Since its launch, Jampack has already processed $500M+ in annualized wholesale volume. $3.2M seed raised, led by Maveron, the VC firm co-founded by Starbucks founder Howard Schultz. Co-founded by Matteo Rossant, who scaled a CPG brand from $0 to $40M in 18 months, and Rezi Tsulukidze (CTO). Based in Brooklyn, NY.

About the Role

Jampack AI is hiring a LATAM-based Founding Engineer-FDE to own the technical integration layer between Jampack and the systems their customers already use. This is a forward-deployed role, meaning you will hop on calls with customers, understand how they use their existing systems, map the data, and build the integrations that make everything work together seamlessly. This is not a standard one-to-one API integration job. Every customer uses their software differently, and figuring out how to connect those systems requires creativity, technical depth, and strong communication.

Jampack's product is only as powerful as the integrations behind it. As the customer base grows, it needs someone dedicated to owning the integration layer so the founding team can focus on scaling the product and closing new business.

You will work at the intersection of enterprise software, supply chain, and AI agents. You will be talking to real customers, solving genuinely complex data mapping and system design challenges, and owning outcomes end-to-end in a space that has barely been touched by modern software.

What You'll Own

  • Own the technical integration between Jampack and customer systems, including ERPs, warehouse management systems, freight platforms, and EDI providers

  • Hop on calls with non-technical customers to understand their current workflows, extract integration requirements, and map system entities

  • Design and execute creative data mappings where systems do not align one-to-one, which is the norm in this space

  • Build event-driven workflows, webhooks, and data pipelines that connect Jampack to the broader customer tech stack

  • Expose frontend components to customers where integrations require a user-facing surface in TypeScript and React

  • Be available on-call for production issues. This is a logistics platform, and things that break after hours can directly affect customer operations

Requirements

Must-Have

Technical

  • 6 to 7 years of software engineering experience with a strong backend focus

  • Proficiency in TypeScript, the primary stack at Jampack

  • Experience building and owning integrations: APIs, webhooks, event-driven architecture, and data mapping

  • Full-stack capability, including React for frontend surfaces when needed

  • Experience with Postgres or equivalent relational databases

  • Familiarity with Supabase or similar backend-as-a-service infrastructure is a plus

Execution and Ownership

  • High agency and creativity can figure out how to connect systems that were not designed to talk to each other

  • Comfortable being on-call for production issues, logistics platforms run around the clock

  • Can own an end-to-end integration from customer discovery call through production deployment without handholding

Communication

  • Excellent written and spoken English at C2 level, required for daily customer-facing work with US-based brands

  • Strong EQ, can translate highly technical problems into clear language for non-technical CPG brand operators

  • Available to overlap with EST time zone during core collaboration hours

Location

  • Remote, Latin America

  • EST time zone overlap strongly preferred, West Coast clients also served, so flexibility helps

Nice-to-Have

  • EDI experience, Jampack is expanding into EDI, and candidates with this background will have an immediate advantage

  • Background in logistics, supply chain, freight, or CPG adjacent software

  • Experience with Flexport, SPS Commerce, or similar logistics and EDI platforms

  • Prior customer-facing or forward-deployed engineering experience

  • Familiarity with Next.js and Supabase

About DualEntry

About the Company

DualEntry is building the OS for finance. Every business needs a financial system of record, yet the world's largest fintech market, worth over $220B, still runs on software from the 1990s. DualEntry's AI-native ERP automates accounting from data entry through close, so finance teams move faster, spend less, and carry less risk. AI is built into the core architecture from day one rather than layered onto a legacy system afterward, which shows up as real-time close, AI-drafted journal entries and reports, anomaly detection, agentic workflows for AR follow-ups and approvals, and next-day migration.

In two years the company has raised over $100M from Lightspeed, Khosla Ventures, Contrary, and Google Ventures, and earned the trust of customers from $5M ARR through to publicly traded companies. The team is 100+ globally with plans to scale aggressively. DualEntry hires outliers, people who have achieved difficult things in their careers or outside them: leaders, athletes who competed at the highest levels of sport, Broadway performers, people who trained with UFC champions, and the founder of the country's largest Python community.

About the Role

The Enterprise AE seat owns the largest and most complex deals in the business, from prospecting through close, on opportunities with multiple economic buyers. Deals run at $100K+ ACV on 6+ month cycles, which is a materially different motion from the mid-market roles. You multi-thread every opportunity across finance, IT, security, and executive sponsors, run deals through MEDDPICC or an equivalent framework, and navigate procurement, security reviews, and legal negotiations through to signature.

This is also a playbook-building seat. You will write the talk tracks, battlecards, and deal patterns the rest of the team runs, own forecasting and pipeline accuracy for your book, and work directly with the founders with real influence over GTM strategy and the product roadmap. DualEntry's enterprise motion is helped by an overlay strategy, sitting on top of existing SAP and Workday infrastructure and reading and writing into legacy systems rather than requiring a full rip-and-replace, which makes the enterprise conversation meaningfully easier than a displacement sale. No territories are defined yet and the ICP is still being refined, so this suits someone who builds process rather than inherits it.

What You'll Own

  • The full enterprise sales cycle from prospecting through close, on complex deals with multiple economic buyers

  • Multi-threading every opportunity across finance, IT, security, and executive sponsors, run through MEDDPICC or an equivalent framework

  • Procurement, security reviews, and legal negotiations through to signature, managing internal teams across the process

  • Pipeline development in partnership with BDRs, identifying target personas within top accounts and customizing outreach, plus forecasting and pipeline accuracy for your book

  • The enterprise playbook itself: talk tracks, battlecards, and the deal patterns others on the team will run, with direct founder access and influence on GTM strategy and the roadmap

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 7+ years in sales, including 5+ years as an individual contributor closing enterprise deals at $100K+ ACV, multi-stakeholder, on 6+ month cycles

  2. Fluency in a formal sales methodology (MEDDPICC, MEDDIC, Command of the Message, or similar) with a track record of applying it to win complex deals

  3. Has sold at early-stage startups, building process rather than inheriting it

  4. Able to navigate procurement, security reviews, and legal negotiations, and to multi-thread across finance, IT, security, and executive sponsors

  5. Entrepreneurial mindset with radical ownership over deals and process, and able to work on-site in New York 5 days a week

Nice-to-Have

  • Experience selling into finance, accounting, or ERP buyers

  • Sold an ERP product end to end (ex-NetSuite, ex-Sage Intacct, and similar)

  • Non-traditional background paired with real finance or accounting experience, which the client is explicitly open to

  • Experience building talk tracks, battlecards, and repeatable deal patterns for a team

  • Sam Bush closed his first deal 28 days after his start date

  • Andy Woods, Head of Product: under his leadership, the team shipped 29 projects and 325+ features in a single cycle, rebuilt bank connections and reporting infrastructure, and launched an AI accounting copilot. Kicked off DualEntry's Ctrl+AI series, walking the company through how we think about building AI-native workflows.

  • David Ryan closed 160% of his quota in his first quarter and was promoted to Sales Manager

  • Base Salary: $150,000 - $200,000

  • Commission: $150,000 - $200,000 (uncapped)

responsibilitiesHtml:
About DualEntry

DualEntry is building the OS for finance. Every business needs a financial system of record, yet the world's largest fintech market, worth over $220B, still runs on software from the 1990s, with no new entrants in 30 years. DualEntry's AI-native ERP automates accounting from data entry through close, so finance teams move faster, spend less, and carry less risk. AI is built into the core architecture from day one rather than layered onto a legacy system afterward, which shows up as real-time close, AI-drafted journal entries and reports, anomaly detection, agentic workflows, and next-day migration.

In two years, the company has raised over $100M from Lightspeed, Khosla Ventures, Contrary, and Google Ventures, and earned the trust of customers from $5M ARR through to publicly traded companies. DualEntry hires outliers, people with a track record of accomplishing difficult things, whether through their careers or achievements outside work. The team includes people who have competed at the highest levels of sport, performed on Broadway, trained with UFC champions, and founded the country's largest Python community, because that is what it takes to reinvent a $220B industry.

About the Role

This is a full-cycle Senior AE seat building DualEntry's UK presence. You own the cycle from lead through discovery and demo to a signed contract, generating the majority of your outbound pipeline, with the balance coming from BDRs, partnerships, and marketing. AEs run their own demos, so demoing a genuinely complex ERP product without solutions consultant support is a requirement, not a preference.

Mid-market deals run on 9- to 12-week cycles, with five- and six-figure ACVs, and are sold to CFOs, controllers, and finance leaders. You will also work with product, feeding what you hear from prospects directly back into the roadmap, and with GTM, partnerships, and marketing to grow inbound. No territories are defined yet, and the ICP is still being refined, so this is a seat for someone comfortable building the motion rather than inheriting one.

What You'll Own

  • The full sales cycle from lead through discovery, demo, and signed contract

  • Self-generated outbound pipeline, which accounts for the majority of total pipeline

  • Your own demos of a complex ERP product, with minimal solutions consultant support

  • Multi-stakeholder mid-market deals on 9 to 12 week cycles with CFOs, controllers, and finance leaders

  • GTM influence, including feeding prospect insight back into the product roadmap

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 3+ years of end-to-end sales experience closing deals in B2B SaaS, full cycle

  2. Has sold to CFO or CTO level, with genuine product complexity behind the sale

  3. Hunter mentality with a track record of generating own pipeline and running outbound

  4. Able to demo a genuinely complex product without solutions consultant support

  5. Quota attainment above 90% for the last 3 years, and able to work hybrid in London 3 days a week

Nice-to-Have

  • Sold an ERP product end-to-end (ex-NetSuite, ex-Sage Intacct, and similar)

  • Sold tooling into finance teams (FloQast, Carta, and similar)

  • Sold a complex technical product at a top tech company (Snowflake, Stripe, Deel, and similar)

  • Curiosity about finance or accounting, which the company will teach

Meet the Sales Team

  • David Ryan has closed 160% of his quota in his first quarter and got promoted to a Sales Manager

  • Sam Bush closed his first deal in 28 days since his start date

  • Wyatt Myers has been building our West Coast presence by organizing events for finance leaders, most recently a poker night that turned attendees into channel partners and warm intros

     

Benefits & Compensation

  • Equity: £30,000 - £40,000

  • Base salary: £95,000 - £125,000

  • Commission: £95,000 - £125,000 (uncapped)

  • OTE: £180,000 - £250,000 

Join now if you want to lock in, do the work, and have the most rewarding role of your career!

— David Ryan, Sales Manager at DualEntry

About DualEntry

DualEntry is building the OS for finance. Every business needs a financial system of record, yet the world's largest fintech market, worth over $220B, still runs on software from the 1990s. DualEntry's AI-native ERP automates accounting from data entry through close, so finance teams move faster, spend less, and carry less risk. AI is built into the core architecture from day one rather than layered onto a legacy system afterward, which shows up as real-time close, AI-drafted journal entries and reports, anomaly detection, agentic workflows for AR follow-ups and approvals, and next-day migration.

In two years the company has raised over $100M from Lightspeed, Khosla Ventures, Contrary, and Google Ventures, and earned the trust of customers from $5M ARR through to publicly traded companies. The team is 100+ globally with plans to scale aggressively. DualEntry hires outliers, people who have achieved difficult things in their careers or outside them: leaders, athletes who competed at the highest levels of sport, Broadway performers, people who trained with UFC champions, and the founder of the country's largest Python community.

 

About the Role

The Senior AE seat targets the mid-market segment and carries the same full-cycle ownership as the AE role with larger and more complex deals. You own the cycle from lead through discovery and demo to signed contract, generating roughly 70% of your own pipeline through outbound, with the balance from BDRs, partnerships, and marketing.

Mid-market deals run 9 to 12 week cycles with ACVs typically between $30K and $60K, and six-figure deals do exist. Some have closed in as little as 24 to 27 days. Buyers are CFOs, controllers, and finance leaders at companies from $10M revenue upward, with the sweet spot around $50M. AEs run their own demos with only one solutions consultant on the team, so demoing a complex ERP product unassisted is a genuine requirement. The ICP is still being refined and no territories are defined yet.

What You'll Own

  • The full mid-market sales cycle from lead through discovery, demo, and signed contract

  • Self-generated outbound pipeline, roughly 70% of total

  • Your own demos of a complex ERP product, with minimal solutions consultant support

  • Multi-stakeholder deal strategy with CFOs, controllers, and finance leaders on 9 to 12 week cycles

  • GTM influence, including feeding prospect insight back into the product roadmap

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 3+ years of end-to-end sales experience closing deals in B2B SaaS, full cycle, with mid-market depth

  2. Has sold to CFO or CTO level, with genuine product complexity behind the sale

  3. Hunter mentality with a track record of generating own pipeline and running outbound

  4. Able to demo a genuinely complex product without solutions consultant support

  5. Quota attainment above 90% for the last 3 years, and able to work on-site in New York 5 days a week

Nice-to-Have

  • Sold an ERP product end to end (ex-NetSuite, ex-Sage Intacct, and similar)

  • Sold tooling into finance teams (FloQast, Carta, and similar)

  • Sold a complex technical product at a top tech company (Snowflake, Stripe, Deel, and similar)

  • Curiosity about finance or accounting, which the company will teach


Meet the Sales Team

  • David Ryan has closed 160% of his quota in his first quarter and got promoted to a Sales Manager

  • Sam Bush closed his first deal in 28 days since his start date

  • Wyatt Myers has been building our West Coast presence by organizing events for finance leaders, most recently a poker night that turned attendees into channel

     

Compensation & Benefits

  • Equity: $40,000 - $55,000

  • Base Salary: $140,000 - $155,000

  • Commission: $140,000 - $155,000 (uncapped)

  • OTE: $280,000 - $310,000

— David Ryan, Sales Manager at DualEntry

Sieve exists to solve the biggest bottleneck in the growth of these applications: high-quality training data.

We've partnered with the world's top AI labs and did $XXM last quarter alone, as a team of just ~25 people. We also raised our Series A from Tier 1 firms such as Matrix Partners, Swift Ventures, Y Combinator, and AI Grant.

As a Machine Learning Engineer at Sieve, this role owns the entire ML lifecycle: understanding customer problems, designing datasets, improving models, building evaluation systems, and shipping production pipelines that deliver measurable improvements in dataset quality.

The work runs directly with frontier AI labs to understand difficult data problems, then builds end-to-end systems that solve them. One week might mean fine-tuning a multimodal model to improve recall on a difficult edge case. The next might mean engineering a VLM-based QA pipeline, designing a new evaluation framework, or running a large-scale filtering pipeline on millions of hours of multimodal data. Sieve is looking for engineers who enjoy owning problems end to end, from customer requirements through shipped production ML systems that measurably improve dataset quality. About the company

Tldr on us: Series B, $91M raised, 7x growth last year.

Digital Transformation gave rise to a $600B consulting Industry. AI Transformation will be 10x bigger and will be delivered through agents. We built that.

Our AI discovers how work actually happens across every team and application, Structures it into a living Context Graph, and improves it continuously.

ServiceNow mapped 900+ processes in 9 days. DoorDash captured 3,800+ finance operations in 14 weeks. That's not a project. That's compounding intelligence.

OpenAI, Google, DoorDash, and Stripe use Within to transform how they transform. We shipped GPT-4 document chat within 12 hours of OpenAI's API launch.

We move fast, reward agency, and care deeply about our customers, our team, and our mission.

About the Role

Within (formerly Klarity) is hiring 2- 3 Staff AI Frontend Engineers who sit at the intersection of product design and frontend engineering. You are an engineer first, but with exceptional design sensibility that elevates everything you build. You will define and implement the look and feel of AI-native workflows, ensuring complex enterprise tools feel as intuitive as the best consumer apps. The product includes a real-time,e WebRTC-powered companion agent that follows users across their screen, generative dashboards that visualize complex enterprise context graphs, agentic chat that operates the web application directly, and a fundamentally new UI paradigm built around generative AI. You will ship at AI speeds, work directly with a tight founding team, and help define the future of frontend SDLC.

What You'll Own

  • Architect scalable frontend systems: design reusable component libraries, establish patterns for state management and API integration, optimize bundle sizes, ensure the platform performs beautifully at scale

  • Own and ship the primary user-facing features users interact with daily, end-to-end from React components through API integration to production polish

  • Bridge AI capabilities with elegant user experiences: partner with product and backend engineers to expose powerful functionality while hiding technical complexity

  • Build complex frontend systems, including real-time WebRTC streaming for the companion agent, generative dashboards, and agentic chat that operates the product itself

  • Use AI tools to rapidly prototype design concepts in code, bridging gaps between teams with working demos instead of static mocks

  • Help define how the team scales code review and SDLC with agents that encode your architectural thinking

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. 6+ years shipping production-grade products. Senior to Staff level.

  2. Mastery of modern web technologies: React, Next.js, TypeScript, Tailwind. You understand the performance consequences of architectural decisions and ship code that's elegant and performant.

  3. AI-native developer. You wield Cursor, Claude Code, v0.dev, Lovable, and comparable tools as extensions of your craft. You ship multiple features per day with AI assistance.

  4. Engineer first, designer by instinct. You discuss Server vs Client Components as fluently as you critique spacing and visual hierarchy.

  5. High agency. You've pushed yourself outside structured environments as a founder, founding engineer, or with significant scope ownership at a real startup.

  6. On the bleeding edge of AI tooling. You can articulate what changed in your stack in the last three months.

  7. Comfortable talking to customers and sales. You shape product through action, not waiting for permission.

  8. Based in SF or willing to relocate immediately. In-person 5 days a week downtown SF.

Nice-to-Have

  • Prior founder or founding engineer experience

  • Real-time WebRTC streaming or video pipeline experience

  • Voice AI product experience

  • Generative UI or generative dashboard work

  • Python backend comfort for occasional cross-stack work

  • No CS or Engineering degree required; portfolio, GitHub, and shipping track record matter more

Within (formerly Klarity) is an equal opportunity employer. Klarity provides equal employment opportunities (EEO) to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, age, disability, genetic information, marital status, or veteran status.

Visa: H-1B transfers accepted; STEM OPT accepted if 2+ years remaining; O-1 not accepted as a candidate's only path

responsibilitiesHtml:
About the Company

Aside is building an AI browser that gets real work done. The product launched virally, already has real users, and is backed by angels, including the CTO of Cloudflare. The team is rethinking the browser interface for an era where an agent, not a person, does much of the clicking, and the product ships on macOS, iOS, and Windows rather than living inside a single web app.

The company is still at founding-team size and ships roughly three features a week across all three platforms. It is a highly design-sensitive product, which means design is not a downstream service function here: it sets the direction of what gets built. Several early hires came directly from the user community, and product taste is treated as a first-class hiring signal.

About the Role

This is the first design hire and a seat on the founding team. The person in this role works directly with the co-founders on everything from feature design to user research, with no design layer above or below them. The scope covers the full surface area of the product across macOS, iOS, and Windows, including the native materials and interaction patterns each platform provides, such as Liquid Glass on macOS and iOS.

Day-to-day splits between three things: living inside the product to find what is broken or missing and proposing design fixes, designing the three or so features that ship each week, and talking directly with users to shape user scenarios. The company is looking for a platform-native designer who thinks in components rather than whole-page layouts, and who is interested in what each operating system makes possible rather than applying a single house style across all of them.

What You'll Own

  • Product design for every feature that ships, at a pace of roughly three features per week across macOS, iOS, and Windows

  • Platform-native experiences on each operating system, composed of native components and materials rather than a single cross-platform template

  • Continuous product audits: using Aside daily, identifying what is broken or missing, and proposing concrete design improvements

  • Direct user conversations and the user scenarios that come out of them

  • The overall design direction of a highly design-sensitive product, working alongside the co-founders

Requirements

Must-Have

  1. Native application design experience across desktop and mobile platforms, with work that composes platform-native components rather than page-level web layouts

  2. A live portfolio website that demonstrates product design depth on its own, submitted with the application

  3. Ability to design and ship at a pace of roughly three features per week on a founding team

  4. Comfort running direct user conversations and translating them into user scenarios and design decisions

  5. Full overlap with PST working hours; San Francisco-based candidates work in person 5 days a week on startup hours

Nice-to-Have

  • Design engineering ability: building a feature end-to-end, or coding interactions and animations (TypeScript)

  • Fluency with platform-native design systems and materials, including Liquid Glass on macOS and iOS

  • Existing users of the product with specific opinions on what to improve

  • A public body of design work, such as an active feed where design work is posted and discussed

--
Work Type: In-person 5 days a week in San Francisco on startup hours, or fully remote from any country. Remote candidates work full PST hours regardless of time zone.
